text:
Campaign Watch Nigeria | Who Gets Counted as a Supporter?

When someone attends a campaign event hoping to take home a generator, on what basis does the campaign count that person as a vote?

Campaign Watch Nigeria put that question to the test. In Abuja, the NDC organised pick-up points to bring people to its event. A photograph from the Kaduna campaign flag-off circulated as far as the South East. By the next morning, a campaign team could report how many buses arrived and how far the photograph travelled. What evidence could it offer that anyone had changed their mind?

In Gombe, speakers pointed to infrastructure and student loans. In Anambra, Peter Obi pointed to rising fuel prices. For a trader paying more each week to move goods to market, which argument carries weight? Did anyone follow up after the speeches to find out?

Then there is the missing voter. A campaign can count every seat on every bus and still know little about the registered voter who stayed home at the last election. Did anyone speak to that voter during those two weeks? What did the campaign learn about why they stayed away and what might bring them back?

Watch Campaign Watch Nigeria, Weeks 7 and 8, from the Political Campaigns Resource Hub. The crowd is in the picture. Who is missing from the count?

#CampaignWatchNigeria #MissingVoter #PoliticalCampaigns  @ResourceHub_HQ @DimphoLekgeu @ICPCampaigns

a friend asked me to check out @buzzchain_io, which you might want to keep an eye on as well. it’s a pseudochain project that converts engagement on x into block production.

the concept is called proof of engagement: posts that mention @buzzchain_io (and meet the criteria, such as receiving at least one like) add weight to the counter. when the counter is full, a block is finalised.

quiet days → slow chain.
busy days → fast chain.

the block time thus serves as a real-time measure of mindshare.

author: cosmos
quoted_text:
5 IBCX test tokens left Zenith EVM Testnet, arrived on Ethereum Sepolia in 88 seconds, and made the return trip in 71 seconds.

That's a completed round-trip transfer through the IBC interoperability pilot developed by the @cosmos team, connecting Zenith to 15 external testnets.

Here's what happened behind those numbers:

1. Burn & Commit: 5 IBCX tokens were burned on Zenith, with the packet commitment recorded in a Canton-finalized transaction in approximately 2 seconds.
2. Verify & Mint: A relayer delivered the packet and verification evidence to Ethereum Sepolia, where the IBC contracts verified the message and minted 5 IBCX tokens.
3. Acknowledge: The acknowledgment returned to Zenith, confirming successful delivery and clearing the packet commitment.
4. Return: The same process ran in reverse, completing the transfer back to Zenith in 71 seconds.

Through Gateway, Zenith connects EVM execution atomically with Canton-native assets and workflows. With IBC, that same EVM environment can communicate with external blockchain ecosystems. Together, they create a path for institutional assets and established EVM-based financial applications to interact across a much broader network landscape.

We've published the full technical walkthrough, with explorer links for every transaction: https://t.co/EFQDd4CRvO

text:
但其实，多Agent技术的历史比这篇论文还要早得多。

众所周知，1973年，MIT的Carl Hewitt等人在《A Universal Modular Actor Formalism for Artificial Intelligence》提出了Actor Model（演员模型）。
这个模型允许不同的计算实体独立运行，通过消息传递进行通信，后来成为并发计算和分布式系统的重要理论基础之一。

到了1975年，卡内基梅隆大学的研究人员已经在Hearsay-II语音理解系统中，让多个负责不同任务的知识模块通过共享信息协作。

1977年，斯坦福大学的Reid G. Smith发表了《The Contract Net》，提出通过类似招标、投标和签约的机制，在分布式系统中分配任务。
简单来说，一个节点发布任务，其他节点根据自己的能力响应，发布者选择合适的执行者完成工作。
这套四十多年前提出的任务分配思路，和今天一些多Agent系统里的Manager/Worker架构，居然有非常明显的相似之处。

到了1997年，Sandip Sen在《Trends in Cognitive Sciences》上发表了一篇综述，名字叫《Multiagent Systems: Milestones and New Horizons》。

当时，多Agent系统已经发展了将近二十年，研究重点也从早期的分布式感知、组织结构和协商协议，逐渐转向协商理论、分布式推理、多智能体学习与通信语言。

也就是说，今天我们讨论的多Agent协作，在1990年代就已经形成了相当完整的学术研究方向。

text:
The beacon of hope came from believing in something. How this tech will be the future of finance, the opportunities to level the playing field for your money, the opportunities to make money as retail etc. The reality is we're deeper into that future we used to imagine. 

It's like when you discover a music artist early but then they go mainstream and early fans keep talking about how they wish that person made music like when they were coming up. The hardest thing to do is cater to your core fans and new fans at the same time. 

I think the gamblefi conversation is bigger because it's not crypto specific, daily fantasy games have been legal for some time now. That was followed with prediction markets which may have started in crypto but have been adopted in the traditional sense by bigger companies the most. Gambling is a problem across the board but only because it's being marketed as a way to supplement income. 

The reality is everyone is looking for more ways to make money because people are struggling. When many of us came into the space, we all wanted to make money too we just paired it with the belief that we are making money through something the world needs. 

I also don't think it's fair to downplay what access to stables and every market in the world 24/7 means for finance and leveling the playing field. 

NFT culture in the early days was amazing because it was about community & money, memecoins gave a similar feeling all while providing things like art, culture and a sense of involvement. Those things have changed a lot by either not being as important or people abusing the tools/market. 

I do think there's a huge opportunity to build that again tho in a new way and attached to great products but that would require companies to spend on culture again too not just does this dollar equal a user or not. We have to take swings at reaching outside our bubble with good impressions. 

The opportunity really is for anyone that feels this way or doesn't like the direction things are moving is to know you have more power than you think if you've been around this industry for a long time, don't lose your voice and go after making whatever change you want to see.

Taking mining to the masses needs to be simple.

text:
「等你们毕业的时候，数学家这个职业可能都不存在了。」

这话是一位顶尖数学家，亲口告诉伯克利一屋子数学博士生的。

说这话的是 Ken Ono，弗吉尼亚大学数学教授、美国数学学会前副主席。

最近 Claude 协助人类数学家证明了困扰数学界 167 年的黎曼猜想，而 Ken Ono 所在的 Axiom Math 此前也借助 AI，仅用 24 天就完成了一项涉及 4310 万行 Lean 代码的庞大数学证明形式化工程。

Ken Ono 昨天在《卫报》写了一篇文章，讲的却是数学家正在经历的另一面。

他自己去年就一度想退出数学。后来加入 AI 公司，总算重新找到了方向。

但问题是，他今年已经 58 岁了，指导过 35 名博士生，几十年的学术积累摆在那里。他当然可以拥抱 AI、转型、重新开始。

那些才二十多岁、刚刚准备把一辈子献给数学的年轻人怎么办？

他在伯克利的那场报告，原定 50 分钟，最后变成了将近两个半小时的学生质询。

有学生愤怒地追问说，你们这些 AI 公司到底准备为我们做些什么？

Ken Ono 没有劝年轻人别抱怨、赶紧学 AI，也没有说什么技术总会创造新工作。

他承认，自己能够成功转型，不代表年轻人也可以。他能保证尊重人类原创贡献、坚持人工审查，但他解决不了年轻人的就业问题。

我觉得这件事最让人难受的地方在于，我们过去一直相信，知识、天赋和长期努力是可以积累的。

你花十年成为数学家，花二十年成为某个领域的专家，这些本领就是你的立身之本。

现在 AI 开始告诉你，可能不需要这么久了，甚至以后根本不需要这么多人了。

问题来了，如果连数学这样最依赖智力、创造力和漫长训练的领域，都不能再向年轻人保证一条相对清晰的职业道路，其他行业凭什么觉得自己能够幸免？

更何况，一个人用了二十年才成为专家，不代表他的下一个二十年，就一定能比机器更有价值。

这才是 AI 时代真正残酷的地方。

我们一直在庆祝 AI 又攻克了哪道人类难题，却很少认真回答那些把青春押在人类智力上的年轻人：

接下来，他们该怎么办？
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
Why I Am Still a Mathematician

On 20 November, Levent Alpöge announced that, working with Claude, he had proved the Riemann hypothesis, a 167-year-old problem about the distribution of prime numbers. The Lean and Mathlib communities have since said they verified the formal proof. We are only beginning to understand the argument, but the news has made a question I hear from students, and have asked myself, more urgent: what kind of future awaits someone beginning a life in mathematics? Last year, I nearly quit.

In May 2025, I led the number theory team for Epoch AI’s FrontierMath Tier 4 project. We wrote difficult research problems to test large language models. I watched an unreleased ChatGPT model compute all the moments of Tamagawa numbers of elliptic curves. Its displayed reasoning drew on work by Manjul Bhargava and Roger Heath-Brown, and on papers my father wrote in the 1960s. I was stunned.

I earned my PhD in 1993, and I did not begin as a confident young mathematician. My adviser, Basil Gordon, and my postdoctoral mentors, Andrew Granville and Enrico Bombieri, helped me find my way. Over the next three decades, I built a life around research, teaching, and mentoring. I still start each day with mathematics on my mind. I’d love to prove that Ramanujan’s tau function never vanishes, or that half of the partition numbers are even.

My 25-year-old self would have been demoralized by what I witnessed last spring, and utterly crushed by the proof of RH. It felt as if the skills I’d spent decades developing could be summoned with just a few keystrokes. I questioned my future and my identity as a mathematician. What would become of my profession and of the students I was preparing to enter it? These questions still haunt me.

Today, I am on leave from the University of Virginia and work as the Founding Mathematician of Axiom Math. I believe in the work I have chosen, and I want to explain why. I’ve been reluctant to offer that explanation. I know that nothing I write will reassure someone just starting a career. What I can offer is an account of what I have learned and the responsibilities I believe come with my choice.

My father’s answer
My father passed away in January. He was a number theorist who introduced me to mathematics long before I could understand any of it. As a boy, I met mathematicians through him at conferences and at dinner parties in our home near Baltimore. He taught me about Ramanujan, the “gift from Kumbakonam” who believed that his family goddess gave him visions of wondrous formulas in his sleep.  As you might know, Ramanujan’s mathematics has shaped my own work.
When I contemplated working on AI for mathematics, I worried that my father would disapprove. I feared that he would see the decision as abandoning something we both loved. Instead, he told me that AI reminded him of Ramanujan.

Ramanujan left discoveries that generations of mathematicians have worked to understand. His notebooks were not simply collections of answers awaiting verification. They suggested connections and questions whose significance became apparent through the work of others. My own mathematical life has been shaped by that continuing effort.

My father saw the possibility that unfamiliar sources of mathematical ideas might again leave us with much to understand. He also recognized how difficult it can be to appreciate mathematics that arrives in an unexpected form. I don’t take the comparison literally. Ramanujan was a human with an extraordinary imagination and an extraordinary life. My father was helping his son think about a future that had become difficult to imagine. His response brought me to tears. It felt like permission to keep being a mathematician in a way I hadn't anticipated.

The work I have chosen
Much of my work now concerns preserving, verifying, and organizing mathematics that others have created. An elegant argument can contain a gap. A hypothesis can be omitted, or two results can use definitions that differ in ways that matter when their proofs are assembled. Carefully examining these arguments can lead to new mathematics. That work deepens my appreciation of the original achievements. It also gives us a way to make them more useful to others.

Formalization provides a new dimension to the practice of mathematics. In a proof assistant such as Lean, definitions, statements, and proofs are expressed in a precise language. A relatively small checking program, the so-called kernel, checks whether a proof correctly arrives at a conclusion from declared assumptions. AI can help construct informal proofs, and a Lean-based proof assistant can check them. We should all value scrutiny that can’t be swayed by one’s reputation. The word “clearly” does not supply a missing justification.
This does not eliminate the need for human judgment.  We must determine whether the formal statement expresses the intended theorem, examine its assumptions and dependencies, and understand its significance. We also depend on the correctness of the checking software.  Also, this work did not begin with AI companies. We depend on the people who developed proof assistants and built libraries such as Mathlib.
Producing a checked proof is part of the task. Organizing the mathematics for all to inspect, understand, and reuse requires further care. I want to contribute to both.

The people teaching me
Last December, Axiom had only a few computers and plastic lawn furniture. The company is led by Carina Hong, one of my former undergraduate research students, and by Shubho Sengupta, a former Meta engineering guru. After spending much of my career helping young mathematicians find their way, I now work for one of them.

Ashvin Swaminathan, another former mentee of mine, recently moved from a Benjamin Peirce fellowship at Harvard to Axiom. Working with him and other research mathematicians has reminded me how much of my mathematical life continues here. We bring different ideas to a problem, question one another’s arguments, and learn from what someone else notices. The pleasure of thinking about mathematics together is familiar.

I’ve learned so much from my interns, including Seewoo Lee and Sidharth Hariharan. Sidharth is well known for his work formalizing Maryna Viazovska’s sphere-packing proof, and he continues to refine the formalization. Seewoo and Sidharth introduced me to the art of formalization. I owe them both so much for their patience and wisdom.

Niels Voss and Vasily Ilin, who sit near me at work, talk math constantly, glued to their monitors as streams of code scroll past. I wish more mathematicians could hear those conversations. Their excitement about the work and their respect for its history are unmistakable.  They are designing the systems that make large formalizations possible. Working with Niels and Vasily has broadened my appreciation for the different forms mathematical creativity can take.

I’ve also been reminded that experience does not guarantee good judgment. When Yifeng Huang first approached me with his ideas connecting the Rogers–Ramanujan identities with geometry, I dismissed them. He persisted. He developed the ideas with Ruofan Jiang (Berkeley) and Alexei Oblomkov (UMass), and eventually I understood enough to recognize their promise. A recent Scientific American account of our collaboration tells this humbling story.

Huang, Kenny Lau, and I subsequently proved their conjecture, with assistance from AxiomProver. Huang had a mathematical vision that I initially failed to appreciate. His collaborators helped develop it, and the technology became useful in solving it. The originality and intellectual ownership of that vision belong to the people who conceived it.

For someone whose father taught him about Ramanujan, that is a lesson. It is easier to celebrate an unexpected idea after it has succeeded than to give it a fair hearing when someone first asks for your attention. I want to become better at the latter.

The mathematics we inherited
Last week we released a formalization of the Classification of Finite Simple Groups (CFSG). Built over decades by a vast community, including Richard Brauer, Walter Feit, John Thompson, Daniel Gorenstein, and Michael Aschbacher, the classification is one of mathematics' great collective achievements. Its announcement in 1983 was followed by substantial further work to address a gap in the treatment of quasithin groups.

We released a Lean formalization based on the first-generation proof. AxiomProver generated corrections and alternative proofs, documented as 96 material departures from the published arguments. Lean’s kernel checks the resulting formal proof.

The project led us back into mathematical research. An obstruction in one route to the Unbalanced Group Theorem required an alternative argument. We’ve been working with Richard Lyons, Ron Solomon, Dan Nakano, and other group theorists to understand the departures from the literature and help others build on the formalization.

The release contained approximately 43.1 million lines of Lean code. That number conveys the scale of the project. Of course, the mathematical achievement belongs to the generations who developed the classification, and our work depends on theirs and on the Mathlib community.

Four Sundays ago, after 24 days of crunching, I sat, pinned to my laptop, watching the final milestones land. When the last one landed, I cried. I thought about the magnitude of the achievement and the people whose work had made it possible. I thought about being a boy my father introduced to group theorists. And I thought about the person I could no longer tell.

Beyond the theorem
Two weeks ago we released a Lean formalization of the Stacks Project.  Johan de Jong began Stacks and developed it with fellow algebraic geometers over two decades. It is a 7,500-page reference for much of modern algebraic geometry. We expect mathematicians to improve and reuse this work, amplifying de Jong’s mission. Researchers building on Stacks should be able to reuse checked proofs of foundational results as they discover and formalize new mathematics.

Developing and refining formalization matters beyond academic research. In our TIME essay, “What Happens When the World Is Run on Code No One Understands?”, Patrick Shafto, Scott Kominers, and I argued for investment in mathematical verification. Formal methods can establish precisely specified properties of software. Deciding which properties matter, and whether the specifications express what we intend, remains a human responsibility.

But identifying a useful application does not create opportunities for graduate students. Training takes resources, research positions require funding, and access to tools is unequal. Nor do the rewarding collaborations I see today establish what the profession will look like as these systems become more capable.

Hope is not a plan
I am 58. I’ve advised 35 PhD students, 17 postdocs, and hundreds of undergrads in REU programs. I’ve had the opportunity to build a mathematical life, with relationships and choices that someone beginning a career can’t assume. I can’t ask a graduate student to regard uncertainty as an adventure simply because I’ve found rewarding work within it.

At a Berkeley colloquium two days after OpenAI announced their Navier–Stokes solution, the room was so crowded that people sat on the floor.  Tensions ran high over credit, transparency, and how mathematicians whose work came first were treated. I told the students that they might graduate into a profession that was shifting under their feet.

A scheduled fifty-minute lecture became a town hall lasting almost two and a half hours. Students asked hard questions about AI companies, including my own. Some asked directly what I was going to do to help students facing the current crisis. Campus security was locking the building as we left.

The student’s question forced me to recognize what I could answer. Finding work that restored my sense of purpose did not tell anyone else where they belonged. This essay is partly an attempt to answer that student, and to take seriously the questions I heard about credit, hiring, training, and who gets to shape the future of mathematics.

Those concerns are not confined to students. The declaration “A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics,” signed by Terry Tao and other Fields Medalists, warns that benchmarks, rushed announcements, and inadequate attribution can undermine the transmission of mathematical understanding. I share those concerns.

I serve on the Mathematical Sciences Education Board at the National Academies, where I recently moderated a panel on the future of work. Those discussions have reinforced my sense of responsibility. At a National Academies meeting, I put my own position this way:
Hope is not a plan, and nostalgia is not mentoring.
I believe both halves. I can say that I’m on NAS subcommittees discussing the future of graduate education and work. We are collecting and compiling expert views on the future of work and education given advances in technology and AI.

Universities, journals, employers, and funding agencies must decide what they support and reward. Students and younger colleagues should participate while those decisions are still open. So should mathematicians who choose to work without AI. In the discussions where I have a voice, I will argue for that participation. My work at Axiom gives me one perspective on these questions. It does not entitle me to settle them for the profession.

Students need opportunities to struggle with mathematics, to make mistakes, and to develop confidence in their own reasoning. They also deserve to learn how to evaluate tools that may become useful to them. Teaching those tools should not become an excuse for neglecting the understanding needed to question their output. In my own advising, I will ask what a young mathematician understood, originated, or made possible. Access to a powerful system is not a substitute for those contributions. I will not treat a decision to work without AI as evidence of a lack of ambition.

For work I help publish, readers should be able to identify what has been proved, what remains assumed, what human review has occurred, and who contributed the ideas and infrastructure. If those distinctions are unclear, I have a responsibility to help make them clear.

These commitments do not solve the employment problem, but they are responsibilities within my reach. I contribute to practical efforts. Our released formalizations, such as CFSG and Stacks, are intended as starting points for future research. Axiom’s work with its partners (e.g. Fields Institute program on arithmetic statistics) brings mathematicians and formal methods together, and our interns and younger colleagues help shape the work we do. These efforts matter to me, even though they cannot answer the larger questions about training and the future of work.

Listening must also leave room for me to change my position. A student who wants to discover mathematics independently is pursuing an ambition I have spent my life encouraging. A postdoc worried about attribution or hiring may see consequences I have missed. A colleague can understand my decision yet still disagree with it.  My enthusiasm should not make those conversations harder.

Why I stayed
I am proud to be a human mathematician. That pride has to do with the people from whom I learned, the students I have advised, and the colleagues with whom I have worked.

My father helped me recognize possibilities that my fear had obscured. Working with a new group of mathematicians gave me something concrete to pursue. Those experiences have renewed my pleasure in mathematics without resolving my concerns about the profession.

I want my students, and their students, to develop ideas that are genuinely their own. I want them to find colleagues who listen, including when an idea first sounds implausible. I want their contributions to receive credit, and I want them to have the material support to pursue a mathematical life.

My current work is one part of how I am trying to contribute. It does not replace my obligations as a teacher, mentor, and member of the mathematical community. I may be wrong about how this will unfold. I am still learning what it means to be a mathematician.

Author’s note: These views do not necessarily reflect those of Axiom Math, the University of Virginia, the National Acad

text:
昨天写了 ethereum:0xa1313eb9f3a445606d9583bcac3ebeb56a858279 的半年复盘，评论里有人问：为什么非要从比特币跨到以太坊？

价格短时间拉了5、6倍，很容易让人觉得项目突然冒出来了，把这半年的东西放在一起看，它其实已经不仅仅是一个比特币隐私币了。

结合项目创始人 @z0r0zzz 的规划，可以把 @tacitfi  理解成：
连接比特币和以太坊的隐私金融设施，在比特币上发行和交易资产，在以太坊侧把私下转钱、换币、做市、借贷做出来。

让 AI 结合项目白皮书画了三张概述图，最简易的方式讲清楚它搭建了什么、今天能干什么，以及下一步想走到哪：

1. 为什么要跨到以太坊？不是单纯换条链炒。

比特币这边，资产发行、隐藏转账金额和原生交易已经有了；普通转账的地址仍然公开。TAC 可以在 BTC 和 ETH 两边跨。

到了以太坊，也不是所有东西挤在同一条链：
👉Tacit Chain 专门处理 TAC 隐私付款；
👉独立的支付池支持 ETH、USDC、USDT 等资产；
👉另有 DeFi 池负责换币、做市和借贷。
这三块要分开看。

2. 隐私，不仅是把币存进去不动。

以 TAC 付款为例，设备先证明这笔钱能付，再把多笔付款打包交给以太坊验证。池内谁付给谁、付了多少，对外隐藏；存入和提现仍是公开的。

ETH 支付池还做出了“装着钱的链接”：比如给海外协作者结算一笔 ETH 报酬，发个领取链接，对方打开后主动领取。

@tacitfi 下午最新发布的 tacit.wei v0.2 演示，又把换币接了进来，USDC 可以换成 ETH 存入隐私池，再换成 SPX，发到一个新地址。

放到支付场景里去理解，即我手里持有一种币，对方想收另一种币，换币和隐私出金可以接起来，减少付款钱包与收款地址的直接关联。

新地址不用提前准备 gas，也不等于免费，刚存就取仍有被关联的风险。

钱放在 DeFi 池里，则还能继续换币、提供流动性，或用 cBTC 抵押借 cUSD（cBTC 这一版，锁 BTC 的人还要额外押一笔以太坊资产作保证金）

3. 下一步真正吸引人的，是把上述操作变得更黑箱且简单。

社区提过一个设想：用户存 USDC，后台换成 BOLD 完成隐私付款，朋友点链接领钱，最后按需取出 USDT。

换个实际商业的场景：客户习惯付 USDC，商家想收 USDT，完成收付款，且不想把整个钱包和生意往来摊在链上给人看。

用户无需费劲的去研究在哪条链、进哪个池，就舒服简单的把钱付出去。这才是我们日常的真实使用需求。

所以接下来重点留意两件事 —— 有没有人反复用它付款、交易？这些使用场景，能给 ethereum:0xa1313eb9f3a445606d9583bcac3ebeb56a858279 带来多少真实的锁定和手续费收入。

这半年，Tacit 证明了自己能把东西做出来。从功能到产品，靠体验；从产品到生意，靠复购和收入。下一步，能不能用真实需求养活自己，才是 ethereum:0xa1313eb9f3a445606d9583bcac3ebeb56a858279 的挑战。

text:
$HYPE vs $ASTER vs $LIT

Despite 2026 being one of the worst years for crypto, perp DEXs are one category that have done really well.

Real fees, real revenue and real usage.

(2026 YTD)

So which one is the best bet from here? We ran every number 👇

1️⃣ What you’re actually buying

Hyperliquid is a chain. Its own L1, own order book, own matching engine, all onchain. You’re buying the toll booth for onchain derivatives.

Aster is a multichain venue. BNB, ETH, Solana, Arbitrum, up to 1001x leverage, stock perps, hidden orders, backed by the BNB orbit. You’re buying reach and features.

Lighter is a zk-rollup. Every match, margin check and liquidation is proven with a ZK-SNARK and settled to Ethereum. Zero fees for retail. You’re buying trust-minimized execution.

Own the rails vs own the reach vs own the proof.

2️⃣ Volume (Hyperliquid, not close)

YTD perp volume:

> HYPE: $2.32T
> ASTER: $735B
> LIT: $657B

Among the three, Hyperliquid is 62.5% of the flow. Aster 19.8%. Lighter 17.7%.

Hyperliquid alone has done ~1.7x Aster and Lighter combined.

3️⃣ The fee take (the most important line on the board)

Now watch what that volume actually earns.

YTD fees:

> HYPE: $804M
> ASTER: $95M
> LIT: $53M

Hyperliquid does 62.5% of the volume but 84.4% of the fees. It earns ~3.5 bps on every dollar traded. Aster earns ~1.3 bps. Lighter ~0.8 bps.

Lighter does 17.7% of the volume and 5.6% of the fees. Zero retail fees is the whole pitch, and it shows up right here.

4️⃣ Usage (read this one carefully)

> HYPE: 300K+ active traders, mostly organic
> ASTER: 2M+ wallets, heavily farm-driven
> LIT: not cleanly tracked

Aster has the biggest user number and the softest one. A lot of it is airdrop farmers recycling capital.

Hyperliquid’s base is smaller but it’s real professional flow.

Lighter doesn’t publish clean active users (or at least we couldn’t find it. If you have a source, please comment).

Open interest and TVL tell the truer story 🤷:

> HYPE: $5.2B OI | $7.2B TVL
> ASTER: $1.1B OI | $719M TVL
> LIT: $564M OI | $697M TVL

Hyperliquid holds ~3x the OI and ~5x the TVL of the other two combined.

Aster and Lighter do similar volume, but Aster carries ~2x the OI. Lighter is turning over its positions much faster.

5️⃣ Who actually pays holders

This is where it splits hard.

Holder revenue, YTD:

> HYPE: $612M
> LIT: $35M
> ASTER: $19M

Hyperliquid has returned more to holders this year ($612M) than Lighter’s entire market cap ($584M).

Look at how much of the fees reach holders:

> HYPE: ~76%
> LIT: ~66%
> ASTER: ~20%

Aster makes ~1.8x Lighter’s fees but pays its holders about half as much.

6️⃣ Price and what you pay for it

As an investor, this is what matters. Hyperliquid leads every stat, but it also has the biggest price tag.

> HYPE: $14.6B mcap
> ASTER: $1.2B mcap
> LIT: $584M mcap

Mcap / YTD holder revenue (lower = cheaper):

> LIT: 16.7x
> HYPE: 23.9x
> ASTER: 63.2x

Mcap / YTD fees:

> LIT: 11.0x
> ASTER: 12.6x
> HYPE: 18.2x

Cheapest on both: Lighter. Most expensive on what holders actually get: Aster.

YTD volume per $1 of market cap (higher = more trading behind every dollar of token):

> LIT: $1,125
> ASTER: $613
> HYPE: $159

Lighter moves the most volume per dollar of mcap on the board. The market just hasn’t paid up for it.

What I’ve seen on CT is a lot of strong personalities backing LIT, and I do believe it’s the most undervalued of the three right now (the stats reflect that too).

7️⃣ Dilution and the overhang

HYPE: $14.6B mcap on $58B FDV
ASTER: $1.2B mcap on $3.9 FDV
LIT: $584M mcap on $2.29B FDV

This is where all three really make my head hurt. Their FDVs and planned unlocks are huge, and we can never be sure how much of it will be absorbed when it unlocks.

A massive massive headache IMO.

✦ What to expect going ahead

The tell is what each token is FOR.

Hyperliquid is a claim on a working, cash-returning near-monopoly. 76% of fees go to holders. The risk is that the price already knows.

Lighter is the value play: cheapest on fees, cheapest on holder revenue, most volume per dollar. But it earns the thinnest fee per trade and has a fat FDV overhang. It has to keep turning usage into accrual.

Aster is the momentum play: huge wallet count and aggressive features, but soft real usage, only ~20% of fees reaching holders, and the richest multiple of the three. It has to prove the flow is real.

Which of these are you holding or planning to buy now? 🤔

text:
fixed-rate, fixed-maturity lending makes sense for RWA credit because the funding now has a defined term. interesting use case for @centrifuge

Midnight provides fixed-rate, fixed-maturity financing. Centrifuge could sit underneath it, managing the asset pool, NAV, cash flows and redemption mechanics.

the structure could look like this:

1. Centrifuge holds the underlying credit assets and manages repayments

2. Midnight provides term financing against the tokenized exposure

3. a liquidity facility covers the gap if financing matures before the underlying assets repay

the risk is the traditional ABCP mismatch: short-term funding against longer-term assets. a fixed maturity tells you when repayment is due, but doesn't guarantee the cash will be there.

Centrifuge V3 already supports asynchronous redemptions, funded escrow and configurable liquidity routes. those mechanics could help manage the asset side, but they don't automatically provide the cash needed to repay maturing paper.

the important distinction is that an ABCP investor has a contractual maturity, while a fund investor may have to wait for a redemption window.

text:
过去一周，黄仁勋的消息持续占据热搜，甚至出现了关于他的 AI 短剧，破圈力度可见一斑。

目前的事态三个关键节点：一是英伟达宣布正式批准黄仁勋辞职；二是公司内部与科技行业联名声援，黄仁勋表示如有需要愿意回归；三是英伟达对外称暂不考虑让他回归。

马斯克评价说，这相当于芝加哥公牛队在连胜赛季中段赶走迈克尔・乔丹。

舆论集中在两个问题：离开英伟达的黄仁勋会怎样？离开黄仁勋的英伟达又会怎样？未来无法预测，但历史可以提供参照系。

一、离开创始人的公司

创始人的直觉很难替代。索尼是最典型的例子。1993 年 11 月，联合创始人盛田昭夫打网球时突发脑出血，虽抢救回来但半身瘫痪。当时索尼正处巅峰：四年前收购哥伦比亚影业，PS 即将发布，Walkman 仍独霸随身听市场。而 Walkman 正是盛田凭直觉拍板的产品 —— 所有调研都说没人会在街上戴耳机，他说 “我不管，就是要做”，最终卖了 4 亿台。

盛田离开后，继任者凡事 “先看市场数据”，创新要经过调研、PPT、委员会层层评审。结果数码时代每一波风口几乎全部错过：MP3 败给苹果，智能手机败给 iPhone 和三星，流媒体几乎缺席。加上部门之间内斗，市值从 20 世纪 90 年代巅峰的近 1500 亿美元跌至 2012 年约 100 亿美元，差点被整体变卖。

那彻底贯彻创始人的作风就行吗？也未必。1966 年 12 月，65 岁的沃尔特・迪士尼因肺癌手术并发症去世，当时加州乐园势头正盛、佛州新园正在选址买地。接班的哥哥罗伊 73 岁、已半退休，几乎完全沿袭沃尔特的做法，甚至把新园命名为 “沃尔特・迪士尼世界”。

前期效果不错，但副作用逐渐显现。公司内部形成习惯：遇到难题就问 “假如沃尔特还在，他会怎么做”。这句话从方法论变成枷锁，动画师不敢有自己的风格，创意会议变成 “他会不会同意”。此后十几年只产出《罗宾汉》《狐狸与猎狗》这类中规中矩的作品，再没有《白雪公主》《小鹿斑比》级别的现象级作品。到 1984 年股价低迷、险遭恶意收购，直到迈克尔・艾斯纳上任，做出《小美人鱼》《狮子王》，才真正走出低谷。

当然不能一概而论。麦当劳一年内换过两任 CEO，业绩几乎无影响 —— 餐饮业相对稳定，加盟商和顾客并不在乎 CEO 是谁。Uber 创始人特拉维斯・卡兰尼克 2017 年被迫辞职后业绩反而大涨，因为他本人丑闻太多，离开是众望所归；新 CEO 上任后公开承认 “我们之前的文化有毒”，该道歉道歉、该整改整改。

共性有两条：第一，所处行业是否变化快到不给时间开会研究、很多决策必须依赖创始人的直觉；第二，客户关系、公司文化、运营模式是否高度依赖创始人本人。而这些因素大多在创立初期就已确定，并非在创始人离开那一刻才出现。

二、离开公司的创始人

这些精英的走向并不都 “理性”，多少受情绪驱使。

最常见的是 “复仇”。人力资源软件公司 Zenefits 巅峰估值 45 亿美元，是当时硅谷成长最快的独角兽之一。2016 年 2 月，创始人帕克・康拉德因 “业务员使用伪造证书” 被董事会扫地出门，投资人当天对他说：“你这辈子不会再有下一家公司了。” 帕克记住了这句话，不到一年就创立 Rippling，做完全相同的业务，直接成为竞品。到 2025 年，Rippling 估值 168 亿美元，是 Zenefits 巅峰的 3.7 倍。他坦言有一半原因是为了复仇，但创立后做的第一件事是确立 “合规优先” 的铁律 —— 用复仇点燃激情，把方向盘交给理性。

也有人一生困在其中。约翰・斯卡利 1983 年被乔布斯从百事挖到苹果任 CEO，那句 “你是想一辈子卖糖水，还是和我一起改变世界” 正是对他说的。1985 年他联手董事会把乔布斯赶出苹果；1993 年，54 岁的他自己也因业绩不佳被赶走。此后反复卷入一堆短命公司，始终想证明 “我也是一个伟大的 CEO”，再没做出过名堂。

也有人留下了正向方法论。金融家桑迪・韦尔 1985 年在美国运通的权力斗争中失败被逐，之后反而主导了多次成功并购。晚年他说，人生中最重要的一年不是创办公司那年，而是被赶出公司那年 —— 它逼他思考：离开公司之后，你个人还剩下什么？

Twitter 创始人杰克・多西 2008 年 31 岁时被董事会以 “管理混乱” 解雇，当天回办公室发现门禁卡已刷不开。四个月后他创办 Square（今 Block），市值一度超过 Twitter。他说，“被赶走的那 4 个月，是我这辈子最想明白的 4 个月”。

三、回到黄仁勋

黄仁勋离开英伟达后会怎样，几乎不可能有确定答案。有人拿他与乔布斯对比，认为都是各自行业的一号人物；但也有人指出，乔布斯被赶出苹果时只有 30 岁出头，黄仁勋今年 62 岁，比桑迪・韦尔被逐时还大 10 岁，而芯片又是门槛极高的行业。把这些因素放进去，“杀回来” 的可能性并不高。

但所有故事有一个共通点：这些人都经历过大风大浪，可再丰富的阅历，在重大变故面前也无法做到绝对理智，心里同样有难受、有不甘。真正厉害的人，是把这些情绪当成动力来源之一，而不是让它当方向盘。最终会做出理性的选择

text:
5 IBCX test tokens left Zenith EVM Testnet, arrived on Ethereum Sepolia in 88 seconds, and made the return trip in 71 seconds.

That's a completed round-trip transfer through the IBC interoperability pilot developed by the @cosmos team, connecting Zenith to 15 external testnets.

Here's what happened behind those numbers:

1. Burn & Commit: 5 IBCX tokens were burned on Zenith, with the packet commitment recorded in a Canton-finalized transaction in approximately 2 seconds.
2. Verify & Mint: A relayer delivered the packet and verification evidence to Ethereum Sepolia, where the IBC contracts verified the message and minted 5 IBCX tokens.
3. Acknowledge: The acknowledgment returned to Zenith, confirming successful delivery and clearing the packet commitment.
4. Return: The same process ran in reverse, completing the transfer back to Zenith in 71 seconds.

Through Gateway, Zenith connects EVM execution atomically with Canton-native assets and workflows. With IBC, that same EVM environment can communicate with external blockchain ecosystems. Together, they create a path for institutional assets and established EVM-based financial applications to interact across a much broader network landscape.

We've published the full technical walkthrough, with explorer links for every transaction: https://t.co/EFQDd4CRvO

text:
하루 만에 주식과 금과 비트코인이 모두 무너지면 누구나 불안해진다. 그러나 질문을 바꾸면 시야가 달라진다. 자산의 가치가 망가져서 빠진 것인가, 아니면 대형 상장과 강제 매도 때문에 일시적으로 현금이 부족해져서 빠진 것인가. 이번 하락은 후자에 가깝다.

​분기점은 예측하는 것이 아니라 확인하는 것이다. 

나는 다음의 신호들을 순서대로 지켜볼 것을 권한다. 가장 먼저 볼 것은 나스닥이 흔들리는 날에도 금이 더 이상 밀리지 않는지다. 이는 현금을 구하기 위한 강제 매도가 끝나 가고 있다는 가장 직접적인 신호다.

다음은 37까지 치솟은 VIX가 20대로 되돌아오는지, 그리고 앤트로픽이 공모가 83달러를 지켜내는지다. 앤트로픽의 공모가는 이번 유동성 흡수의 상징이자 AI 투자 심리의 바닥선이다. 마지막으로 12월 점도표가 제시하는 2027년 금리 경로, 연말 단기 자금 금리의 급등 여부, 그리고 1월 회의에서 연준이 인상 사이클의 종료를 확인하는지를 보면 된다.

대응의 원칙은 단순하다. 

강제 매도로 시작된 하락은 팔아야 할 물량이 다 나올 때까지 며칠, 길게는 몇 주 더 흔들리는 경우가 많다. ‘많이 빠졌으니 오른다’는 생각으로 신용이나 대출을 끌어 한 번에 들어가는 것은 이번 하락을 만든 바로 그 레버리지의 반대편에 서는 일이다. 반대로 분위기에 휩쓸려 멀쩡한 장기 자산을 최저점 부근에서 던지는 것도 피해야 한다. 같은 날 함께 떨어졌다고 같은 이유로 떨어진 것은 아니다.

지수는 밸류에이션 구간에 따라 분할 매수 강도를 조절하고, 금은 하락세가 잦아드는 것을 확인하며 나눠 담고, 비트코인은 전체 자산에서 감당할 수 있는 비중 안에서만 다루는 식으로 자산별 원칙을 분리해야 한다. 그리고 장기 국채의 비중은 안전자산 선호현상에 따라 급격히 하락할 때 추격 매수를 지양하는 것이 재정 주도 국면의 기본값이다.

넓은 유동성의 기차는 여전히 달리고 있고, 좁은 유동성의 배관이 잠시 막혔을 뿐이다. 그 배관이 다시 뚫리는 시점은 12월 FOMC에서 시작해, 늦어도 1월 FOMC에서 확인될 것이다. 지금 투자자에게 필요한 것은 바닥을 맞히는 용기가 아니라, 분기점을 확인할 때까지 살아남는 인내다.

역사는 언제나 그렇게 모두가 확신을 잃은 순간이 장기 투자자에게 가장 좋은 출발점이었음을 보여 주었다.

text:
A IA não tá tirando o emprego inteiro de ninguém. Tá tirando a parte repetida dele.

E em algumas profissões essa parte já é quase tudo.

Atendimento
> IA: responde dúvida, abre chamado, faz follow-up
> humano: caso grave, fraude e empatia
> a Salesforce foi de 9 mil pra 5 mil pessoas no suporte

Tradutor
> IA: texto, legenda, conteúdo em vários idiomas
> humano: interpretação ao vivo, tradução juramentada
> 1º lugar no estudo da Microsoft de profissões onde a IA mais se aplica

Assistente administrativo
> IA: e-mail, agenda, planilha, resumo
> humano: exceção e coordenar pessoas
> o Fórum Econômico Mundial projeta -20% até 2030

Contador
> IA: lançamento, conciliação, relatório padrão
> humano: estratégia tributária e assinar embaixo
> 3ª profissão mais exposta à IA no Brasil, segundo a ESPM

Programador júnior
> IA: escreve, corrige e documenta código
> humano: arquitetura, segurança e decidir o que construir
> o emprego de quem tem 22-25 anos nas áreas expostas tá 19% abaixo do esperado (Stanford)

Redator e designer
> IA: rascunho, variação de peça, revisão
> humano: voz própria, gosto e direção de arte

Enquanto isso, as funções que mais crescem até 2030 são especialista em Big Data (+113%), engenheiro de FinTech (+93%) e especialista em IA (+82%).

Em resumo, quem só executa tarefa repetida tá na fila. Quem aprende a comandar a IA tá do outro lado.

text:
Providers’ data-handling claims have mostly relied on self-attestation. This isn't going to be sufficient.

Just as continuous benchmarking and monitoring transformed the quality and reliability of inference both on and out of OpenRouter, we expect technical validation, auditing, and continuous testing to do the same for data policy enforcement.

Encrypted TEE (Trusted Execution Environment) inference will be a great way for providers to accelerate this.

We will keep raising the bar, and providers that want to be on OpenRouter will need to meet it.
author: matthew_d_green
quoted_text:
Security researchers recently found data-handling problems with some inference providers available on OpenRouter. The findings showed no breach of OpenRouter itself.

In response, we’ve off-boarded 3 providers, removed many endpoints from ZDR eligibility, and notified affected customers.

We’re now building the researchers’ testing into ongoing checks. Full update and provider write-ups on our blog: https://t.co/AjtVbHKsim

text: An extraordinary comment by a President of a country, that I never seen before. Pres. Bukele of El Salvador has written an eulogy on 3 members of his rescue forces that died in an accident in Haiti that is intimate, dignified  A meditation on the real purpose in life.
author: nayibbukele
quoted_text:
Hoy quiero hablarles de tres héroes salvadoreños que perdieron la vida mientras cumplían una misión lejos de nuestra patria.

Tres miembros de nuestra Fuerza Armada que viajaron a Haití con un propósito: rescatar a cuatro de sus compañeros que habían sido secuestrados por pandillas haitianas.

Lamentablemente, una explosión accidental durante esa misión les arrebató la vida.

Sus nombres son: el teniente Cristian Daniel Palacios Santos, el cabo Emerson Alexander Zepeda Zelada y el cabo Wilber Manuel Serrano Medina.

Conocí de primera mano la valentía del teniente Palacios Santos. Durante un operativo, en un momento crítico en el que unos contratistas privados abandonaron sus posiciones, el teniente tomó el control de la situación y actuó con rapidez y determinación, logrando salvar varias vidas, entre ellas las de sus propios compañeros.

Todos aplaudimos su valentía.

Recuerdo que en ese momento pensé: “Este muchacho llegará lejos. Tiene todo el temple y la capacidad de un líder”. Jamás imaginé que, poco tiempo después, estaría entre los fallecidos en un accidente.

También me informaron del extraordinario valor de los cabos Zepeda Zelada y Serrano Medina. Durante unas pruebas en El Salvador, una granada quedó atorada en un dron. La batería estaba por agotarse y no era posible dirigirlo hacia una zona completamente segura para que se estrellara. Serrano Medina sostuvo el dron a aproximadamente un metro y medio del suelo mientras Zepeda Zelada desactivaba manualmente la granada.

Sabían perfectamente el inmenso riesgo que estaban corriendo, pero aun así decidieron actuar para proteger a los demás.

Y lo lograron.

Estas no son simplemente historias sobre tres héroes. Son acciones que nos permiten entender quiénes eran estos hombres: militares capaces, valientes y comprometidos con una misión que siempre pusieron por encima de su propia seguridad.

Varias veces he dicho que siempre he admirado a las personas que deciden dedicar sus vidas a salvar las de otros. Porque hay algo extraordinario en ellas. Algo que no es natural, que no es común, que no es normal.

Todos los seres humanos tenemos una reacción instintiva ante el peligro. Si vemos un peligro, huimos de él. Si hay un incendio, corremos y tratamos de alejarnos. Pero un bombero no huye del incendio, hace lo contrario, lo que casi nadie más haría, y en lugar de huir del incendio, corre hacia él, arriesga su vida, camina entre las llamas si es necesario para salvar a los demás.

Eso no es algo normal, es algo extraordinario.

Si escuchamos una balacera, nuestro instinto es huir de los disparos, buscar refugio, mantenernos alejados. Pero un policía hace lo contrario. Ellos no huyen de los disparos como haríamos todos, van hacia ellos, sacan su pistola y corren hacia el peligro para salvar a los que están en él.

Eso no es algo normal, es algo extraordinario.

Lo vimos con los rescatistas que enviamos a Venezuela, salvadoreños abriendo túneles en estructuras inestables que podrían colapsar en cualquier momento. Nuestro instinto natural es huir de un edificio que se desmorona, pero nuestros rescatistas hacían lo contrario: entraban a esas estructuras, sabiendo que podían morir ahí adentro, para salvar a quienes estaban atrapados.

Eso no lo haría casi nadie, mucho menos por un desconocido, pero ellos sí, porque los rescatistas, al igual que los policías, bomberos y militares, reaccionan de una manera totalmente diferente a todos los demás. Ellos no huyen del peligro, van hacia él. Eso es difícil de entender para la gente normal, pero ellos no son gente normal, son gente extraordinaria.

Cuando los demás retroceden, ellos avanzan. Sabiendo perfectamente que eso puede costarles la vida misma.

Y no es que no tengan miedo, es que hay algo más fuerte que ese miedo: su deseo de salvar a los demás.

Esa es la vocación que mueve a nuestros militares, a nuestros policías, bomberos y rescatistas. Personas que han decidido dedicar sus vidas a proteger la de los demás…

text:
每年固定节目，给大伙分享我这一年每天都在用的不错 Mac 软件，由于有了 AI 以后反而常用软件少了很多，只有这 24 个了，看看哪些是大伙也经常在用的，也欢迎推荐你认为 2026 你最喜欢的软件给我。

打算想到啥说啥，先看到哪一个说哪个，不按照下图顺序来给大伙分享。

1. Mole：几乎每天会用来清理一遍垃圾以及看菜单栏看系统的状态，包括里面的卸载、不息屏、风扇小工具每天会使用，同时每天都会来迭代它。

2. Claude Code：我现在主要用 CLI，几乎每时每刻都在跑，默认Opus 5.5 high，复杂 就 Fable 5.2 medium，现在没有用 Codex 了，也没有用啥多 Agent 工具，我喜欢简单可控的编码。

3. Kaku：我喜欢简单默认好看轻量的终端工具，每天在上面多 Tab 跑 Claude，我喜欢用黑色背景的 TUI 搭配  JetBrains Mono 代码字体，这个字体依然是我最近三年最喜欢的代码字体。

4. ego lite：今年最让我惊喜的一个浏览器，简单漂亮好用，之前我主要是用 Helium Browser，假如你很少用 AI 操作浏览器，那我还是推荐 Helium 这个，轻量迅速简洁，ego 这个我喜欢的点，就有给 Agent 一个单独的窗口，不会干扰我自己的使用。

5. 1Password：今年把我的密码管理逐步迁移到了这个，多平台复用，整体软件品质不错，更多是在 AI 什么都可以破解的年代求一份安全保障，价格是也可以接受，用习惯以后，感觉还挺好用的。

6. 妙言：一个轻快的原生的 Markdown 笔记应用，默认好用好看，在支持 iPhone 版本后，我几乎每天会打开记录一些东西，每周大伙看到的潮流周刊就是我用这个 Mac 端来编辑的，包括大伙看到的我的所有文字输出，都是在这个里面草稿来的。

7. Grok Bot：可能不是每一个小伙伴喜欢用这个，我感觉他帮我了我很多产品经营增长上的忙，包括各种答疑、退款处理、记录问题到 Notion，以及我每天的投资报告、推特日报、潮流日报，均来源于这个帮我在做 Personal Agent。

8. UU远程：我感觉这个产品简单易用，在我外出的时候，非常依赖他帮我操作家里的多 Mac 和 Windows 设备，给我帮了很多忙，虽然后面也做付费了，不过我还是非常希望他家可以越做越好。

9.  Apple Music：用过非常多音乐播控器，我还是最喜欢苹果自带的，包月也便宜，歌的质量也高，我听的歌也都在上面，而且我喜欢这个简洁，以及多设备使用，不太喜欢花里胡哨的东西，这个刚刚好。

10. Pake：一个可以很简单把网页打包成桌面 App 的工具，我会把微信读书、李志音乐播放器打包成 Mac 应用，然后用 raycast 快捷键唤起，很方便，而且可以按照自己喜好定制非常多的东西。

11. Shottr：假如要推荐一个最好用最简单的截图工具，还是推荐这个，貌似才4 刀不买好像也可以用，轻量、我非常喜欢用他来截图窗口、以及滚动截图，用了好几年了。

12. 微信输入法：我的所有设备都是用这个输入法，腾讯的赎罪产品，简洁舒服、打字猜的准，特别是最近的语音输入法，我不想装同类的软件，就只用这个，非常好用。

13. Parallels：这个软件可能对大伙也褒贬不一，但是我感觉还是这个 Windows 虚拟机做得最好用，也可能是我 M5 Pro 的缘故，我在上面用，完全没有虚拟机的感觉，非常顺滑，在我开发 Windows 软件的时候帮了很大的忙。

14. Bob：一个随手用的翻译工具，好像也不贵，然后绑定了自己的 AI key，设置快捷键以后，随用随唤起，很不错。

15. Input Source Pro：默认切换输入法的工具，比如在你写东西的里面默认就是中文输入法，在你敲代码的地方默认设置英文，少掉了一次快捷键切换，润物细无声。

16. NetNewsWire：轻量默认好用的 RSS 阅读器，也有 iPhone 版本，推荐使用我自己做的妙言主题，很舒服，这是我认为在 AI 时代还需要保持阅读的一个很好工具。

17. Sketch：哈哈好吧，我承认我现在的所有的设计、做 Logo 、做稿子，还是用这个软件，可能是原生客户端的缘故，有执念，而且工具完全够我用，也比较舒服，可能是用习惯了，反而不太关注新产品。

18. Top Calendar：菜单栏最好用的日历时间插件，可以把系统的菜单栏时间替换后用这个，点击可以看到日历，以及你的日程，也是润物细无声。

19. AyuGram：开源易用简洁的电报工具，可以把原有官网的版本很多会员广告啥的干掉，然后有非常多自定义的功能，但是默认其实就够了，平时我每天打开1-2次看看消息。

20. Stash：我在用的 Mac 和 iPhone 的代理工具，用了2年左右了，胜在稳定和原生，以及满足我使用的覆写、DNS 覆盖等功能，然后家里 Apple TV也用的这个，我认为最好的就是多设备配置同步，省去了我来回配置的麻烦。

21. Raycast：这个是唯一我感觉有点重但是也每天在用的工具，同步也在另外一台电脑上使用 Tinycast，作为对照使用，Raycast 的粘贴历史记录、软件快捷键唤起、文件快捷键查找这几个功能我几乎每天用，就是麻烦一点第一次使用，你要关掉非常多我认为多余的功能才会好用，Tinycast 等更成熟了，可能主力机就迁移过去了。

22. uPic：用了好多年的图片上传到 cdn 的工具，为啥用这个，还是原生轻量的执念，绑定好快捷键以后，我认为非常好用。

23. Command X：一个非常轻量的让你的 Mac 在访达支持剪切的工具，就这个功能，哈哈哈。

24. VS Code：前 AI 时代每天都在用的，现在也经常用，主要用来看一些 diff，以及整理一些文件内容，以及看 README，不过我感觉明年我可能就不用这个了，找一个更轻量原生的。

text:
If you want to know how AI will change software security over the next two years, look at crypto’s early days.

Early DeFi was open-source contracts holding huge amounts of money, often unaudited and readable by anyone. Every day was hack day. If money sat in code someone could read, attackers had every reason to find the bug.

Some teams tried to hide by not verifying their contracts, betting nobody would bother reading raw bytecode. It bought time. But unverified contracts still got exploited, and even MEV bots running private strategies got drained.

AI is now bringing the same problem to traditional software.

When a model can analyze a patch diff, reverse-engineer a binary, or understand decompiled bytecode, hiding the source code stops being a barrier. Work that once took skilled researchers days can now be done by machines at scale. And when there’s money in finding bugs, attackers will use them.

Web2 is less ready for this than it thinks.

Crypto made source code review part of shipping. Most web2 security testing is black-box: probing running applications from the outside. Ask a web2 hacker to do a source code review and they’ll look at you funny.

We’ve seen this firsthand. When we opened up a source code review of a 23,000-line web application with $30K in rewards, the scarce resource wasn’t money. It was web2 researchers trained to read source code. Our smart contract audit competitions regularly draw over 900 researchers.

AI is already finding zero-days in traditional software. When AI agents scanned 2,849 recently deployed smart contracts, the only new bugs they found were basic mistakes in small tokens worth less than $4,000 combined. That’s a limited study and doesn’t prove crypto is more secure. But crypto learned early that code holding money attracts people willing to inspect every line, and built audits, bug bounties, and continuous testing around that fact.

The rest of software is about to learn the same lesson. The next two years will be rough. Now is the time to take security seriously and fix everything that shipped with zero security reviews.

我顺手查了一下论文的作者，也挺有意思。

第一作者盛步云，1964年出生，当时在武汉理工大学从事机械制造与自动化研究，1997年开始攻读博士，2001年晋升教授。
后来他一直在研究智能制造、工业软件、数字化工厂等技术，还承担过国家重点研发项目。

第二作者杨明忠，1943年出生，1966年毕业于华中工学院，是武汉理工大学机械工程领域的老教授，曾经担任机电工程学院院长、博士生导师。
他在1978年就获得了赴欧洲学习的机会，1980年在国际期刊发表过挑战当时美国相关技术标准的研究。

所以这篇论文其实来自两位研究机械工程、工业软件和智能制造的学者。

他们当时想解决的问题也很实际：如何让计算机自动规划制造工艺，并通过多个智能体分工协作，提高系统的可靠性和灵活性。

第Ⅰ部「数学の道具箱」は、記号と論理のことば、順序・半順序・束、変化率・勾配・内積、二階微分と強凸性（「本物の谷」の条件）、積分と割引・終端項、πc標準形と価値関数、指数収束とGrönwallの不等式、距離と不変集合（「檻」と「部屋」の数学）、縮小写像と固定点、逆極限、エントロピー・散逸・相互情報量、確率とマルコフ連鎖、形式体系とゲーデルの二つの定理、しきい値の数学、条件付き相互情報量と「選べる」、述語と定義、記号早見表の十七の道具で、学校で習った数学から第二巻の数式までをつなぐ。

第Ⅱ部「定理案内」は、定理20「象徴は心に向きを与える」、定理21「偏った棚は、本物の谷を作る」、定理22「消さずに、包んで、上がる」、四法印の定理23〜26、定理27「無明と行は同値である」、定理28〜31、そして定理32「条件32-A〜Cのもとで、閾値を超えれば未来TCZへ指数収束する」まで、定理ごとに、物語で入る、定理が言っていること、①〜⑤の一枚まとめ、数式解説版の該当章の全文再録、中心式をほどく三段箱、数で確かめる、証明の心、この定理が言わないこと、つながり、確認問題、日常への含意、まとめを備える。

序部・道具・各定理の章・終部には、式を使わずに主張の形を描いた図解（図解1〜38）を置き、どの図解にも読み方を添えた。終部は十三の定理を一つの物語として読み直し、仏教の言葉が使われる理由（証明したことと証明していないこと）、教育・組織・情報環境への含意、よくある誤解の十の問答を扱う。

本書テーマのひとつ仏法定理化は、思想を含む認知活動のモデル化に加え、釈迦の論理を数理的に厳密に確認することは、今後の仏典研究の重要な方向性の一つになると認識している。それほど仏教教理は緻密である。

本巻は刊行出来る予定の第三巻に続く。本来非公開の「コグニティブリサーチラボ研究報告」背景論文もKindleからリンクで読者が読めるようにした。これは過去の第一巻、第二巻でも更新すればリンクで読めるようにした。背景論文をAIに読ませれば数式が苦手な人もAIが更に細かく解説してくれるはずだ。

AIに本書を更に解説させる場合は、文献のリンク先の全てのコグニティブリサーチラボ研究報告論文を先に読ませる必要がある。これらを読ませずに解説させて誤読されている例を複数聞いている。

第三巻もほぼ書き上げた。第三巻との接続の厳密性を維持するために既刊の第一巻、第二巻も僅かに修正したので第一巻、第二巻もKindleの手続きに従って更新して欲しい。更新は無料。自動更新設定になっていれば近々に更新されるはず。

学術版の数理をそのまま読めた人も『第二巻 公式解説ガイド付き完全版』を、仏教やコーチング、リーダーシップ等に関わるこれまでの自身の知識を一切使わずにまずはありのままに読んで欲しい

text: 不仅是Dario，整个Anthropic高层的理念都很奇葩。比如负责给模型培训道德、制定了“Claude宪法”的Amanda Askell，早年曾经跟她的前夫William MacAskill合写过一篇评论，主张可以把所有食肉动物全部杀掉，从而最大程度地减少动物界的苦难总量。想象一下把这个思路延伸到人类上……
author: minglaugodel
quoted_text:
刚看完《华盛顿邮报》和《华尔街日报》最近扒出的 Anthropic 一大堆内部奇观，这家公司已经不是一般的抽象了。

首先，Dario 曾经头顶一整条面包去参加开发者会议。

对，你没看错。面包，顶在头上。没人知道这哥们到底在干什么。

更有意思的是，Dario 每两周都要给全公司开一次叫作「Dario Vision Quest」的大会，拿着长篇文档，给员工讲 AI、人类文明、战争、政治，还有他对世界末日的理解。

公司甚至把 Dario 一篇长达 14000 词的 AI 宣言印成实体书发给员工，内部有人管它叫「小蓝书」。

还给员工发过一批帽子，上面写着「Good luck, everyone」，祝大家好运。这也是 Dario 给自己的思想大会收尾时爱说的一句话。

好家伙，末日预言、领袖著作、定期布道，周边产品都齐了。

那怎么才能加入这个组织呢？

Anthropic 有一套专门的「文化面试」，应聘者要提前读 Dario 写的文章，再接受价值观考察。

一位落选者收到招聘经理的短信，经理自己都形容，这面试有点像在问你：「准备好加入邪教了吗？」

公司早期员工还会互相写「如何与我共事」的操作手册。员工自称 Ants，也就是蚂蚁；Dario 当年带着一帮人从 OpenAI 出走时，那群人还有个绰号叫 Pandas，熊猫。

公司搞团建也很离谱，把三米高的书架搬到户外草坪上，搭出阅读角，让大家一起玩游戏、编友谊手链。

但最吓人的其实是他们脑子里那套东西。

《华盛顿邮报》挖出一份 Dario 2022 年的内部备忘录。他当时估计，AGI 有 20%～30% 的概率导致人类毁灭或文明永久停滞，危险程度甚至可能超过核武器。

与此同时，《华尔街日报》还披露，Dario 当年在 OpenAI 工作时，曾经在 Slack 讨论过一个非常赛博朋克的设想：

如果 AI 抢走大量工作，引发社会动荡怎么办？

「沉浸式电子游戏，或许可以缓解由此产生的政治冲突。」

还有更有意思的。

Dario 以前写涉及敏感 AI 技术的文章，甚至要用完全断网的电脑，写完打印出来，生怕信息泄露。

而 Anthropic 内部真的发生过泄密事件。据前员工向《华盛顿邮报》透露，公司去年因为内部 Slack 信息外泄展开调查，泄密者最终被开除。

Dario 随后还在内部大会上表示，自己不会因为泄密而闭嘴。为了证明这一点，他甚至直接骂当时的英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋贪婪。

在这样的内部文化下，Anthropic 已经不满足于只教育自己的员工了。

《华盛顿邮报》还发现，他们开始把学者、智库研究员和媒体人士请进公司，安排为期两天的思想交流。参加者要阅读 Dario 的文章，以及长达 23000 词的 Claude 宪法。

其中就包括向外界解释他们对 AI 安全、地缘政治，以及限制中国获得先进芯片的看法。

这一切背后有一条特别完整的逻辑：

AI 可能毁灭人类，所以人类需要我们。

我们需要更强大的 AI 才能保护人类，所以我们必须继续开发。

为了确保人类安全，我们需要更多算力、更多资本、更多政治影响力，以及更大的权力。

于是，一家坚信自己正在制造人类末日风险的公司，一路冲到了万亿美元市值，还培养出一大批身价上亿的员工。

这套理论好像永远都能自圆其说。

Anthropic 真正擅长的不是训练 Claude，而是把一家商业公司的野心，包装成一场拯救人类的道德事业。

世界是否真的需要救世主，我不知道。

但这群人显然已经把自己当成救世主了。

纳指短期有反弹需求，但并未见底，后续大概率先寻底，再修复，重返前高需要时间。

为什么重点看纳指？因为 bitcoin:native 本身的泡沫已经挤掉，后续跌多少，跌多久，美股说了算！

从周线看指数已跌破2025年以来的加速上升趋势线，从高点回撤约17%，市场正式进入估值压缩阶段。

当前结构与2022年有相似之处：通胀粘性、高利率和美债收益率上行共同压制科技股估值，区别在于，美国经济仍有韧性，AI也已形成真实订单和盈利，因此出现系统性崩盘的概率有限。

但四大云厂商资本开支持续膨胀，市场接下来会严格审查AI投入能否转化为利润，单靠讲故事已经撑不起高估值。

未来半年，纳指大概率围绕24000-29000点宽幅震荡，短期先看24000-25000点能否形成周线支撑，守住后有望反弹至27500-29000点；若跌破23000点，调整将进一步指向21000-22000点长期趋势线，这也是我认为纳指能跌倒的极限位置！

AI长期趋势没有结束，但估值泡沫需要时间消化，未来半年最可能走出先跌后稳、反复筑底的行情，急跌可以观察，反弹不宜盲目追高。

反应到BTC上就是跌中有反弹，反弹中多次磨底，如果纳指不破新低5开头的BTC基本就是底部，即使纳指继续跌20%到21000点附近，BTC大概率跌倒4.8万附近我认为也足够了！

quoted_text:
Hoy quiero hablarles de tres héroes salvadoreños que perdieron la vida mientras cumplían una misión lejos de nuestra patria.

Tres miembros de nuestra Fuerza Armada que viajaron a Haití con un propósito: rescatar a cuatro de sus compañeros que habían sido secuestrados por pandillas haitianas.

Lamentablemente, una explosión accidental durante esa misión les arrebató la vida.

Sus nombres son: el teniente Cristian Daniel Palacios Santos, el cabo Emerson Alexander Zepeda Zelada y el cabo Wilber Manuel Serrano Medina.

Conocí de primera mano la valentía del teniente Palacios Santos. Durante un operativo, en un momento crítico en el que unos contratistas privados abandonaron sus posiciones, el teniente tomó el control de la situación y actuó con rapidez y determinación, logrando salvar varias vidas, entre ellas las de sus propios compañeros.

Todos aplaudimos su valentía.

Recuerdo que en ese momento pensé: “Este muchacho llegará lejos. Tiene todo el temple y la capacidad de un líder”. Jamás imaginé que, poco tiempo después, estaría entre los fallecidos en un accidente.

También me informaron del extraordinario valor de los cabos Zepeda Zelada y Serrano Medina. Durante unas pruebas en El Salvador, una granada quedó atorada en un dron. La batería estaba por agotarse y no era posible dirigirlo hacia una zona completamente segura para que se estrellara. Serrano Medina sostuvo el dron a aproximadamente un metro y medio del suelo mientras Zepeda Zelada desactivaba manualmente la granada.

Sabían perfectamente el inmenso riesgo que estaban corriendo, pero aun así decidieron actuar para proteger a los demás.

Y lo lograron.

Estas no son simplemente historias sobre tres héroes. Son acciones que nos permiten entender quiénes eran estos hombres: militares capaces, valientes y comprometidos con una misión que siempre pusieron por encima de su propia seguridad.

Varias veces he dicho que siempre he admirado a las personas que deciden dedicar sus vidas a salvar las de otros. Porque hay algo extraordinario en ellas. Algo que no es natural, que no es común, que no es normal.

Todos los seres humanos tenemos una reacción instintiva ante el peligro. Si vemos un peligro, huimos de él. Si hay un incendio, corremos y tratamos de alejarnos. Pero un bombero no huye del incendio, hace lo contrario, lo que casi nadie más haría, y en lugar de huir del incendio, corre hacia él, arriesga su vida, camina entre las llamas si es necesario para salvar a los demás.

Eso no es algo normal, es algo extraordinario.

Si escuchamos una balacera, nuestro instinto es huir de los disparos, buscar refugio, mantenernos alejados. Pero un policía hace lo contrario. Ellos no huyen de los disparos como haríamos todos, van hacia ellos, sacan su pistola y corren hacia el peligro para salvar a los que están en él.

Eso no es algo normal, es algo extraordinario.

Lo vimos con los rescatistas que enviamos a Venezuela, salvadoreños abriendo túneles en estructuras inestables que podrían colapsar en cualquier momento. Nuestro instinto natural es huir de un edificio que se desmorona, pero nuestros rescatistas hacían lo contrario: entraban a esas estructuras, sabiendo que podían morir ahí adentro, para salvar a quienes estaban atrapados.

Eso no lo haría casi nadie, mucho menos por un desconocido, pero ellos sí, porque los rescatistas, al igual que los policías, bomberos y militares, reaccionan de una manera totalmente diferente a todos los demás. Ellos no huyen del peligro, van hacia él. Eso es difícil de entender para la gente normal, pero ellos no son gente normal, son gente extraordinaria.

Cuando los demás retroceden, ellos avanzan. Sabiendo perfectamente que eso puede costarles la vida misma.

Y no es que no tengan miedo, es que hay algo más fuerte que ese miedo: su deseo de salvar a los demás.

Esa es la vocación que mueve a nuestros militares, a nuestros policías, bomberos y rescatistas. Personas que han decidido dedicar sus vidas a proteger la de los demás…

quoted_text:
Speaking of stop losses, some people have been asking me to share related books and videos. I haven't organized them yet, so here are the absolute basics. 

First, for stop losses, you'd better have a major premise, which is defining your maximum loss per trade and maximum daily loss. There is a tool called a Risk Manager.

There are many types of stop losses. The most common ones are price and structure stops, such as trendlines, swing highs and lows, and market structure shifts, as well as capital and drawdown stops (a fixed dollar amount per trade such as ≤ $500, a fixed equity percentage such as risking ≤ 1% of total capital per trade, and a total account drawdown percentage).

Others include volatility stops (ATR multiple stops such as entry price ± 1.5×ATR, Bollinger Band and VWAP standard deviations such as ±2σ, and options implied volatility (IV) expected moves), time stops (closing the position if price fails to clear the cost basis after N bars, closing before the end of a specific session such as the first 30 minutes of the US market open, and closing options early to avoid Theta decay), order flow scalping stops (absorption failure, liquidity pulls, and extreme Delta divergence), and trailing stops (where the stop line moves in the same direction as unrealized profits and locks in gains against reversals, which can be divided into fixed point trailing, percentage trailing, and volatility based trailing such as the Chandelier Exit, which is the highest high minus N times ATR).

Also, a stop loss doesn't necessarily mean closing the entire position. Scaling out is also a form of stop loss. Most commonly, you size your position based on a pattern, so conversely, if the pattern you are trading deteriorates and no longer matches your expectations, you can scale down your position.

Also, many trading platforms or custom plugins now feature a Risk Manager, which you can use as a reference to design your own risk management: max daily loss limit, max daily profit lock, account equity trailing drawdown, max position size limit, max order size per trade, max daily trade count, max consecutive losing trades, no opening positions without a stop loss along with restricting the user from manually canceling stop orders or dragging stops significantly wider into a loss, ATR dynamic position size reduction, order book depth and spread auto circuit breakers, and automatically switching to reduce only mode or flattening all positions at T minus 5 minutes before high impact news events. 

In reality, the risk management we normally use is just a behavioral guardrail. The biggest difference between institutions and retail traders is that institutional risk management goes beyond behavioral guardrails into strategy level hedging. I won't get into the complex institutional strategy side since it's unnecessary for regular trading, though you can try hedging with 0DTE options or relative strength hedging.

quoted_text:
刚把多个 Claude 账号在本地和 T3 Code 里彻底打通了，太爽了！！！

多个账号随时切，Codex 也可以这么搞

Claude 直接走 Anthropic 官方自带的 CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR 机制，零中转零反代，不怕封号，而且两个号完全共用一套配置

我把整套合规配法，给大家详细讲一讲：
1、用官方变量新建第二个号 默认的 ~/.claude 完全不动，终端直接跑： mkdir -p ~/.claude_second && CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude_second claude auth login
变量只设 CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR，动了 HOME 钥匙串就读不到了

2、软链接共用同一套配置：
刚建好的新文件夹里面是空的，自己攒的全局 CLAUDE.md、Skills、Hooks、插件和记忆全读不到
直接把 ~/.claude_second 里的 CLAUDE.md、skills、settings.json、plugins、projects 全部软链接指回 ~/.claude，以后改规则、装新技能只改一处，多个号同时生效

唯一没法直接链的是 .claude.json（里面混着账号信息和个人 MCP），让 AI 写几行脚本只把里面的 mcpServers 同步过去就行

3、接进 T3 Code 看多份额度：
在 T3 Code 的 Settings > Providers 里再加一个 Claude 实例，Binary path 填 claude，目录填 ~/.claude_second

配好后按 Cmd+U 看限制页，多个号的 5 小时和每周额度会直接拼在同一条里分段显示，开新线程时哪边有余量选哪个

text:
US net equity inflows are up to ~3.0% of GDP, their highest on record in data going back to the 1980s.

Net equity inflows measure foreign purchases of US stocks minus US investors' purchases of foreign equities.

This figure has risen nearly +5.0 percentage points since the 2022 bear market low.

Meanwhile, net debt inflows, which measure foreign purchases of US debt securities, such as Treasuries minus US purchases of foreign debt securities, are down to ~1.8%, their lowest since 2022.

As a result, net equity inflows have surpassed net debt inflows as a % of GDP by the widest margin since the 2008 Financial Crisis.

In other words, foreign investors are increasingly directing money towards US equities rather than US bonds.

Overseas demand for US equities has never been this strong.

text:
Ethereum has settled on one design principle for privacy. To keep the base layer neutral.

The protocol ships the mechanisms. Inclusion lists stop block builders from dropping private transactions. Encrypted ordering keeps a transaction sealed until its position in the block is fixed. The terms of privacy get set higher up.

EthSystems' guide for banks reads well against that split. Who can open the record? Can you freeze one client's holding? These are policy questions. If you run a bank, you answer them. The chain stays out of it.

Specifically in Asia, this is much needed because each regulator answers those questions its own way. Japan wants holder names and addresses in a register. Korea moves fund registers onto depository-screened ledgers from February 2027. Hong Kong's SFC wants extra controls before a fund touches a public chain.

Now each of these are contestable judgements that will change as law and norms change. Exactly why none of them belongs in a hard fork.

the greatest buying opportunities always show up when they seem least obvious.

Collector Crypt's gacha volumes have dropped significantly. so did the solana:CARDSccUMFKoPRZxt5vt3ksUbxEFEcnZ3H2pd3dKxYjp price.

I think a few things clearly aren't priced in, which is why I believe this is one of the most undervalued onchain businesses in the industry right now:

- these charts only show onchain revenue. as the partner network building on their API grows and they verticalize the whole stack, a growing share of the business happens offchain. that's hard to verify from the outside, but in my view the business is doing better than these charts suggest.

- you think Ripmart is priced in. it isn't. people understand the value proposition, but hardly anyone grasps the scale of what's being built. I expect it to onboard a huge number of users within the first few weeks, most of them without even realizing they're onchain. probably the single most important thing for the business and its marketplace, and the market gives it zero credit.

- the indices were announced in the worst possible market and sentiment, so they were mostly overlooked. I'd also argue most people don't yet understand what they'll look like and why it potentially even could grow into their most profitable offering. together with Ripmart they're a gamechanger: they broaden the product suite and make the business less dependent on gacha revenue alone, which has been the biggest question mark for more conservative investors.

to sum it up: even on these sharply lower numbers, they still generate more than $70M in annualized net revenue, with one of the most profitable, obsessed and sharp teams in the space.

on top of that, more than a third of the supply sits in the treasury, and the team has confirmed those tokens only enter circulation for something clearly accretive to the business, like strategic acquisitions.

adjust for that and the effective valuation is around $200M imo. the market is pricing in the worst case for solana:CARDSccUMFKoPRZxt5vt3ksUbxEFEcnZ3H2pd3dKxYjp, a Pokémon bubble bursting and revenue in decline, but none of the biggest catalysts and bull cases.

2. Il cochait la case stratégique que tout le monde surveille

Qui est la défense face aux puces maison des hyperscalers. Chez Arm, il travaille directement avec Meta, Google et Amazon et connaît par cœur l'architecture des CPU de Nvidia. C'était le profil idéal pour protéger les marges et garder les gros clients dans l'écosystème

3. Le marché n'aime pas le vide, voir le déteste

text:
OpenAI 公布的困惑度曲线里，显示了一次模型训练范式转换。

GPT‑4.5（~0.877）是 pretraining 做大 base model 终点。之后 o3，困惑度反而回升到 ~0.90。

倒退的原因在于 post-training：RL 要跑大量 rollout，成本和基座大小成正比。用更小的基座做大量 RL 更划算，于是算力从预训练流向了后训练。

而 RL 本身不降低困惑度。它把输出分布收窄到高奖励的模式上，提升的是能力，牺牲的是对整体文本分布的拟合。

但后训练会间接反哺基座。RL 之后的强模型可以生成合成数据、推理轨迹和干净的代码，喂给下一代做预训练或 mid‑training。

后训练不直接降低困惑度，但它通过造数据的循环，间接让基座变强，所以看到了 2026 年困惑度的骤降。

黄仁勋因多起婚外情指控（包括涉嫌与一名疑似中国情报人员保持关系）被迫离开英伟达。但两位熟悉董事会内部讨论的知情人士指出，真正推动解职的最核心导火索，是他在多个问题上的“缺乏坦诚”与“撒谎”。

早在 2025 年 10 月《纽约时报》曝光英伟达与新加坡数据中心 Megaspeed 的业务往来后，董事会成员就曾当面质询过黄仁勋与 Alice Huang 的关系，黄仁勋当时对董事会予以否认。

直到今年 11 月 8 日，他才被迫承认婚外情，随后其与一名直接下属的不正当关系也接连浮出水面。 知情人士对 WIRED 表示，Alice Huang 到底是不是间谍，董事会当时根本无法坐实；但能够确定的，是黄仁勋长达一年的撒谎，“这是一个关乎诚信与信任的根本问题”。

连日来，董事会主席 Harvey Jones 一直在极力平息关于黄仁勋可能回归的讨论，强调其行为严重违背了公司政策与治理准则。 哪怕特朗普公开呼吁“他是个天才，道个歉应该获得第二次机会”，马斯克与数千名员工也高呼其重掌帅印，董事会依然没有松口。

而在英伟达内部，员工同样充满焦虑与不解。 在全员大会上，临时 CEO  Colette Kress 坦言员工最关心的就是股价下挫和解职黄仁勋的决定。尽管她将员工加薪窗口提前来安抚军心，但对调查细节和审议结论守口如瓶。 

一位在英伟达工作的资深计算机科学家向 WIRED 直言：“整艘船已经沉了，但管理层却根本不打算公开究竟发生了什么，整个公司现在就像一个密不透风的黑盒子。”

text:
The most revealing number in Kraken’s USD 17,000 bitcoin trade was 73 Canadian cents. That’s what one US dollar bought on the exchange later that Saturday morning.

At the low, bitcoin traded for CAD 24,250, roughly USD 16,900 at Friday’s exchange rate. About 10.7 bitcoin:native changed hands below the equivalent of USD 20,000 in that 15-minute window. Kraken’s own dollar market was trading near USD 57,700 when the low printed.

By 09:40 UTC, Kraken’s prices told a remarkably consistent story. Convert its BTC/USD price at its own USD/CAD rate and you got CAD 42,200 per bitcoin. The last trade on BTC/CAD was CAD 42,557. The two routes agreed to within 1%.

For an outside check on Kraken’s price, @VantorMarkets is a good place to start. Use its USD/CAD rate to convert its BTC/USD quote into Canadian dollars, then compare the result with the price BTC actually traded at on Kraken’s CAD market.

Using the Bank of Canada’s Friday rate of CAD 1.4325 per US dollar, Kraken’s 09:40 BTC/USD price worked out to about CAD 82,800. A buyer who already held CAD on Kraken still saw a deep discount. A buyer starting with USD and sourcing CAD on Kraken gave up most of that discount on the currency conversion, before buying any bitcoin.

For onchain lenders, the trap is treating the direct price and the local cross as independent confirmation. Both reflected the same premium on Canadian dollars inside Kraken. That discount belongs in a stress test for collateral that must be sold through that book. Applying it to a loan that can be unwound directly in USD would make the borrower pay for an exit the protocol never needed to take.

text:
【Chinese Spy：无威胁的性别 + 有威胁的族裔 = 被观赏的仙女棒】

Chinese Spy 的帖子看多了，今天来开麦，讲讲我觉得不适的地方。

一个很残酷的真相是，在西方当权者的眼里，Chinese 有威胁性，女人没有。

在传统的权力结构与地缘政治叙事中，不同身份所承载的「威胁感」是不对等的。当人们谈论一个国家或一个种族的威胁时，潜意识里预设的主体往往是男性。

▪️在当下的国际博弈语境里，「Chinese」代表着实质性的竞争与威胁。

哪怕黄这样已经做到天花板级别的人，在地缘政治博弈和党派博弈面前，依然随时可能被推出来献祭，不仅被夺走最珍视、最宝贵的东西，还要被所有人围观和评判私德。

▪️但「女人」，在宏观权力结构中，往往被视为不具实质威胁的群体。

因为女性整体掌握的核心政治与社会资源相当有限（且实际上并不存在真正的女性同盟），所以当权者甚至可以容忍女性表达诉求、甚至给予一定的发声出口。

只要这些声音没有真正触及核心利益的重新分配，就可以被视为无害的情绪释放（除非你社会影响力太大了🤷）

▪️而当你同时是「Chinese」又是「女性」时呢？

故事又不同了。

这不是简单的「少数族裔 + 女性」身份的叠加，这中间藏着更深层的交叉性（Intersectionality）。

西方文化里对亚裔女性有种根深蒂固的「超女性化」滤镜，觉得你是顺从的、迷人的、没有攻击性的。所以当一个女生用性感自拍去套用「Chinese Spy」这个词时，原本充满敌意和政治危险的间谍，就被去威胁化了。

没错，你只是在 AI 链条连环爆炸用来转移矛盾的时候，顺便燃起的一支仙女棒 —— 因为你同时是失权的女人，又是可以被献祭的少数族裔，但你实在美丽动人，所以你燃烧的样子非常适合被观赏。

————————————————

当然，退一步讲，我完全理解这种自我符号化的选择。

大家都活在注意力经济里，个体的玩梗本质上就是为了获取流量，提升自己的商业价值。

女性主义走到第三波/第四波之后，变得越来越个体化，极其强调个人主义、主体性、自我赋权这些层面。

对于美丽的亚裔、拉丁裔这些少数族裔女性来说，身上本身就带着「女性+少数族裔」的双重少数身份，在西方视角的凝视里很容易被性感符号化。

既然被凝视是逃不掉的，那顺水推舟利用这种「自我符号化/自我东方化」带来的注意力去换取流量和实际利益，在这个时代似乎成了一种非常常规、甚至算得上聪明的选择。

而且，我认为我在网上看到的这些博主，并不是真的对政治不敏感。

相反，正是因为她们有足够的敏感度，才精准踩中了受众的兴奋点。与其试图去推翻凝视的规则，不如选择直接掌控凝视的杠杆，把刻板印象转化为实实在在的流量。

————————————————

博主们拿到了流量，用他者歧视自己的武器，来为自己制造社交货币。

但问题在于，这个世界的代价和红利可不是由同一批人承担的。

在真实世界的另一端，还有很多少数族裔的女性，正在学术界、职场、生意场上真刀真枪地打拼。

我相信她们刷到这些玩梗的帖子时，内心是非常难过的，并且她们实际上才是真正要承担这些「间谍」指控和审查代价的人。

（传播学里管这叫「代表性的负担」——少数群体的个体行为，往往会变成整个群体的画像。）

我并不是想指责任何一个具体发自拍的女生，每个人都有在规则里谋求个人利益的自由。但无论如何，把这些玩梗背后潜在的权力结构摊开来讨论，绝对是有意义的。

我希望大家能意识到这个梗背后的深层问题。

我也支持更多这些严肃的讨论。

text:
The first practical solution to witness encryption for general NP:

https://t.co/ERxhHz4Qvo

At 100 bits security: ciphertext size: <8 GB, encryption and decryption time: seconds. Formally lean verified from standard security assumptions (bi-linear generic group and random oracle model under Module-SIS.) 

This work is built on recent feasibility results by Hair and Sahai and improves their ciphertext size and encryption time by 10 orders of magnitude and decryption time by 6 orders.

Our motivation is non-interactive proof verification on Bitcoin without the need for challengers and operators, but witness encryption is a fundamental problem and we hope this work will open up many other use cases.

text:
I think there’s a huge opportunity in data collection hardware for Physical AI.

UMI, DexUMI, YAM and data gloves have made a lot of progress, but this is far from solved.

A few things that really matter here:

Data quality: accurate motion tracking, everything staying in sync, and reliable touch and force data

Usability: can someone actually use it for hours without getting tired or constantly recalibrating?

Scalability: how easy is it to collect data across different tasks and environments?

Transferability: does the collected data actually improve robot performance in the real world?

Durability: does the hardware hold up after months of daily use?

Economics: what does one usable hour of data cost, not just the hardware?

There’s still a lot of room for innovation here.

I remember when I was in Prépas (France's 2-year competitive program to access elite engineering schools), we naively dreamed of solving the Riemann hypothesis like an amateur footballer dreams of lifting the World Cup one day.

Just like in amateur football, most of us knew we had no chance. But the few of us who still believed in themselves tried to make it to ENS Ulm, so that maybe one day, their name would be read in the books like Fermat, Gauss or Poincaré.

With the advent of AI, what dreams are left for these students today? I don't know, but maybe, just maybe... the era of solving problems is dead. Upon us is the era of defining problems that are worth solving. And that has always been a much harder task anyway.

Dream on... until the next model is released!

text:
To
The Chief Administrator  
Shree Jagannath Temple Administration  
Temple Office, Grand Road  
Puri – 752001  
Odisha  

Subject: Earnest Appeal for the Immediate Resumption of Continuous Spiritual Devotional Music along the Sacred Grand Road (Bada Danda) from Shri Jagannātha Temple to Shri Gundicha Temple  

Respected Sir,  

With profound reverence for Lord Shri Jagannātha, the Lord of the Universe, and with deepest respect for the sacred traditions entrusted to the Shree Jagannath Temple Administration, I most humbly address this letter.  

It has come to the notice of countless devotees that the continuous broadcast of spiritual and devotional songs dedicated to Shri Jagannātha — which for long years filled the air along the holy Grand Road (Bada Danda) between the main Temple and the Shri Gundicha Temple — has been discontinued. This sacred thoroughfare, sanctified by the annual journey of the Lord during the Rath Yatra and by the footsteps of innumerable saints, seers, and ordinary devotees across centuries, once resonated day and night with the divine names, kirtans, and bhajans of Mahaprabhu. That living stream of sound has now fallen silent.  

The continuous playing of these pure, traditional, and elevating compositions was never mere background music. It served as a gentle, ever-present reminder of the Lord’s presence; it softened the hearts of pilgrims; it protected the spiritual atmosphere of the Bada Danda from the encroachment of worldly noise; and it offered solace to the weary, the aged, the poor, and the visiting devotee who might otherwise walk the three kilometres in spiritual silence. In the living tradition of Odisha’s bhakti, from the immortal verses of Salabega to the sankirtan of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and the unbroken lineage of Jagannātha-seva, such continuous remembrance of the Divine Name has always been regarded as a form of service in itself.  

I therefore most respectfully and urgently request the Temple Administration to restore this blessed practice without delay. May the speakers once again carry the pure, traditional Odia and Sanskrit bhajans and kirtans of Shri Jagannātha along the entire stretch of the Grand Road, day and night, as before — not as entertainment, but as a continuous offering of sound to the Lord and a spiritual gift to His devotees.  

Such a restoration would be an act of great kindness and foresight. It would preserve an intangible yet precious aspect of the living heritage of Shrikshetra, strengthen the atmosphere of devotion that surrounds the Temple, and give quiet joy to the countless hearts that still long to hear the Lord’s name while walking His sacred path.  

I place this appeal before you with folded hands and complete faith in the wisdom and devotion of the Administration. May Lord Shri Jagannātha, the ocean of mercy, guide every decision taken in His service.  

With deepest respects and sincere prayers,  

Yours faithfully,  

Jai Shri Jagannātha Mahāprabhu

The first practical solution to witness encryption for general NP:

https://t.co/ERxhHz4Qvo

At 100 bits security: ciphertext size: <8 GB, encryption and decryption time: seconds. Formally lean verified from standard security assumptions (bi-linear generic group and random oracle model under Module-SIS.) 

This work is built on recent feasibility results by Hair and Sahai and improves their ciphertext size and encryption time by 10 orders of magnitude and decryption time by 6 orders.

Our motivation is non-interactive proof verification on Bitcoin without the need for challengers and operators, but witness encryption is a fundamental problem and we hope this work will open up many other use cases.

text:
This is going to get a bit nerdy, lets do it because I want to explain why you actually want people arbing onchain equities

In TradFi, a market maker can sell you a stock on one venue and buy it back on another to hedge. If the stock is cheap on one venue and expensive on the other, firms trade that gap until the prices come back in line. You  buy the stock, then the firm on the other side can trade it hundreds of times and finish the day roughly flat. This is literally the job of the market maker is to provide liquidity

In this case you have three tokens (Ondo, Securitize, Backpack) backed by the same stock and still trade at different spreads. If I’m market making Anthropic, I care who I can sell the token to and what I get back when I redeem it. Securitize, Ondo and Backpack handle that differently

With Securitize, you complete KYC to buy a brokerage entitlement backed 1:1 by Anthropic shares. If you want dollars back, you can sell through the broker for USDC. If you want to send it to me, my wallet has to be KYC'd too. Even if we agree on a price, you can only deliver the token to me after I’m onboarded

Ondo’s international stock tokens move more like USDC or USDT. Wallets can receive the stock backed token without opening an Ondo account. KYC comes in when you mint or redeem directly. Ordinary redemptions pay out in stablecoins. A market maker can still hedge the stock elsewhere, but only separately approved institutions can redeem the token in kind and receive the underlying shares through Alpaca

We’re investors in Backpack at Frictionless, and the part I think is underappreciated is that Backpack also runs the brokerage. Once the token is on Solana, wallets can trade it without a Backpack account. An eligible individual with a verified brokerage account can move in both directions. Buy the stock and withdraw it as tokens, or deposit the tokens and get the stock back

In-kind redemption is the alpha here. Say I’m a market maker. I buy 100 tokens from you onchain and sell 100 shares from my brokerage account to hedge. With Backpack, I can redeem those tokens and put the 100 shares right back in my account. If redemption pays me in stablecoins, I still have to go buy 100 shares to get back to the same position. That extra trade can mean crossing the spread again, and the stock can move between fills. I have to leave room for that in my quote, which means a lower bid for you

Now flip the trade. Say you want to buy Anthropic onchain. Anthropic is being offered at $100 in the brokerage while the stock market is open, and the cheapest offer on Solana is $101. One market maker can sell to me at $100.50, buy the stock at $100 and withdraw more tokens to replace what they sold. Another can offer me $100.25 and win my order. I get a tighter spread, and they can quote me more size because they know where the next shares are coming from

You can see this in the Blockworks data. Across seven stocks, Backpack had a cheaper round trip than xStocks in 98% of matched Jupiter quotes for $500 to $10k orders. In other tests of $1 to $100 SpaceX trades, the average all-in cost was 0.11% on Backpack versus 4.29% on Robinhood chain. Roughly 40x as much on Robinhood chain once fees were included

The market structure and redemption matter quite a bit and its how better execution turns into more volume. If I show up with $10k of USDC on Titan, Jupiter or DFlow my order routes through whoever gets me the most stock

text: Better governance prevails.
author: BillAckman
quoted_text:
I believe the @nvidia board is not acting in the best interest of shareholders nor in a manner consistent with their fiduciary duties. 

What we know is that the board fired Jensen or forced his resignation for violating company policy and/or in response to the accusation of an affair with a spy. 

They did so without careful consideration of the impact on the company, its customers, its shareholders or other stakeholders. 

They rushed to judgment without the benefit of careful due diligence or even with a basic understanding of the facts. 

How do we know this? 

We know this by how quickly Jensen was fired and how little was known at the time of his firing. 

It takes time to convene a board meeting.  There was time, maybe, for one Zoom. 

And this is a decision that should have been made by a board sitting in person and carefully deliberating the facts once they are known.  

And they should have slept on the decision and met again the day after to discuss the facts, the risks and the other implications of their decision. 

The timing and lack of information did not allow for careful board deliberation. 

While boards can fire a CEO for an inappropriate relationship with a subordinate, it should not be an automatic decision. That is why we have boards comprised of humans and not agents. 

A board should consider whether or not such a relationship was consensual or whether it was an abuse of power dynamics. And a board has to consider what the impact of the firing is on all stakeholders. 

If I were in this board, I would not have rushed to judgment based on articles in the media. I would have made sure the board had all of the facts so it could make a careful and informed decision. 

Boards of Delaware companies have a duty of care which means they must make informed, prudent and good faith decisions. This clearly did not happen here. 

What law firm is advising this board?  

Or is the board even taken good legal advice? 

It doesn’t look like it. 

And now the board is compounding its failures by insisting that there is no possibility for Jensen’s return as CEO. 

Why is it in the best interest of the company to foreclose the possibility of Jensen’s return and to do so before all of the facts are known? This is yet another breach of their duty of care. 

Furthermore, the board has launched an investigation whose scope is unknown. Investigations can be extremely damaging to a company and should be carefully targeted to address whatever facts need to be known rather than be overly broad in scope. 

In short, this looks like a series of major governance failures by directors that panicked due to headlines in the media. They likely felt compelled to do something because they were afraid of looking bad in the media, not because it was the right thing for them company. 

They couldn’t stand the heat. 

The board’s conduct here is shocking for a company of this scale and importance to our country and the world at large, particularly at this moment in history.
