🌅 
                       “The Crimson Threshold”

The disk burned low and perfect against the layered veil, its edges softened by miles of air yet its heart refusing every invitation to fade. 🌅 Each ray traveled farther than reason demanded, scattering the cold blues until only fire remained, and the horizon itself seemed to lean forward as if testing the weight of what approached. Darkness gathered in the foreground like an audience that already knew the ending yet stayed seated, waiting for the moment the light would prove them wrong. Every particle of atmosphere bent the path, lifting what should have fallen, turning geometry into a circle so clean it felt less like accident and more like declaration.

The world below held its breath in shades of blue and gray, the hills reduced to silhouettes that could not interrupt the descent. 🔥 What rose from the earth was not mist alone but the accumulated weight of every unspoken thing, every half-truth that had lingered through the long day. Still the disk continued, its lower curve meeting the line of the land without flinching, as though the meeting itself had been rehearsed since the first rotation. Cameras would later flatten the intensity into a single tone, yet the eye that watched knew the core still pulsed beneath the bloom, unrecorded and undiminished.

No hand reached to steady it. No voice called it back. ✨ The light simply occupied the space it had always occupied, indifferent to the stories built around its absence. In that stillness the distance between observer and observed collapsed into a single shared breath, the kind that arrives only when something larger than preference insists on remaining visible. The haze did not obscure so much as reveal the length of the journey each photon had taken, every scattering a quiet accounting of how far truth must travel before it is allowed to arrive.

Those who turned away called the color unnatural. Those who stayed felt the temperature of the air shift against their skin and understood that color was only the visible remainder of what had been stripped away. 🌌 The disk neither argued nor explained. It occupied the threshold between what had been and what would continue, its outline sharp enough to cut through every claim that the sky was merely backdrop. Night waited, patient and certain, yet the fire held its place one breath longer than calculation allowed, and in that extra breath the entire arrangement of the evening rearranged itself around the refusal.

When the last visible edge met the dark line, the glow did not vanish. It spread outward into the upper layers, staining the clouds the color of metal just before it cools. ☀️ People would later describe the moment as ordinary, a sunset like any other, yet the ordinary had never demanded so much of the air or left so clear a mark on those who watched without blinking. The disk had done nothing unusual. It had simply continued.

The Crimson Threshold is the line where the day surrenders its name yet keeps its heat, where the perfect circle meets the imperfect earth and neither yields first. ⚡ In that meeting the watching world is forced to decide whether the light was ever meant to be believed or merely endured, and the choice itself becomes the only history that remains after the disk has gone. What follows is not darkness alone but the memory of a shape that refused to break, a heat that outlasted the angle of its arrival, and a silence wide enough to hold every question the sky was never required to answer. The threshold stays. The fire does not apologize for remaining visible until the final possible instant. Those who saw it carry the outline behind their eyes long after the horizon has returned to ordinary gray, and the carrying itself becomes the continuation no photograph can finish.

quoted_text:
Nvidia's board has listened.

It has been a long 14 days, but we are pleased to see Nvidia's, $NVDA, board agree with our view to reinstate Jensen Huang.

From day one of this controversy, we maintained a firm view:

The door for Jensen Huang to return should never have been closed without a thorough and independent investigation.

Despite the board explicitly ruling out his return just days ago, we remained firm in this view.

This weekend, something clearly began to change behind the scenes, as we highlighted just 14 hours ago.

President Trump called for Jensen Huang's return, US Treasury Secretary Bessent said the door was open, and Attorney General Todd Blanche said he has "certainly" not concluded that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy.

Today, the leader of the AI Revolution is back.

Congratulations to all!

text:
Imagine founding a company worth $6 trillion, losing your job over an affair, watching $3 trillion disappear from its market cap and getting your position back just 11 days later.

That’s what happened to Jensen Huang, the founder of Nvidia.

And this has to be the craziest corporate comeback we’ve ever seen

Jensen co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and spent the next 33 years turning it into the most valuable company in the world.

By October 6, 2026, Nvidia shares had reached an all-time high of $243.37, giving the company a market capitalization of $5.9 trillion.

Insane right, I know, but Jensen had a problem, and everything changed on November 8.

Nvidia announced an independent investigation following reports that Huang had been involved in two extramarital relationships.

One involved Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s VP of healthcare, who reported directly to him.

The other involved Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based company that purchased Nvidia processors and was reportedly under scrutiny over suspected connections to Chinese intelligence.

Wild.

Huang acknowledged his infidelity to employees, but the potential national security implications made the situation much bigger

Just four days later, on November 12, he resigned as Nvidia’s president, CEO and board director.

Colette Kress became interim CEO, while Harvey Jones took over as chairman.

Keep in mind that this was the same man who had been running Nvidia since its foundation in 1993.

The market absolutely hated his departure.

By November 16, Nvidia had fallen to $156 per share, while Donald Trump publicly supported Huang’s return and a petition calling for his reinstatement collected more than 177,000 signatures, including one from Elon Musk.

But here we need to look at what happened on November 17.

Nvidia reported its Q3 FY2027 earnings, and the numbers were ridiculous:

$115.8B in quarterly revenue
103% year-over-year revenue growth
$65.3B in net income
$130B in projected revenue for the following quarter

During the same earnings call, Huang offered to return as CEO.

Nvidia’s board rejected him, again.

Three days later, on November 20, Nvidia shares collapsed another 14%, closing at $125.53.

From its October peak, the company had lost $2.85 trillion in market capitalization.

But here we are, November 23.

Donald Trump publicly called for Huang to be rehired, saying it would be the best decision for Nvidia and the United States.

Hours later, Nvidia’s board unanimously voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, CEO and board director.

Within minutes, Nvidia shares pumped 30% in premarket trading, recovering $900B in market capitalization.

All happened in 11 days.

Full Nvidia Press Release

NVIDIA Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board Director

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board. The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. 

“We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.” Harvey Jones will remain as Board chair.

“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.” 

As previously announced, in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, the Board formed a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate, and the committee retained independent counsel to assist it in that investigation. The Board reiterated that the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion. Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it.

The Board also recently formed a National Security and Export Control Committee comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks. The committee is engaging counsel with experience in national security matters, and such counsel will be retaining advisors with expertise in national security matters. NVIDIA is commencing a search to fill a new position, Chief Compliance Officer, to oversee compliance across NVIDIA and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries.

text:
This morning’s rally may look impressive, but this is exactly why I covered the shorts. The market had gotten oversold enough to produce a rip-your-face-off rally. After capturing nearly 7R on the downside, there was no reason to overstay the trade.
That said, keep this morning’s action in perspective. A number of stocks are up a whopping 10%-30%, but most are barely a blip on the charts. For now, they’re counter-trend rallies in stocks that are still in significant downtrends, particularly in Technology.
The S&P 500 fell 11.6% from its October 6 record high, the first 10% correction since the February-April 2025 selloff, but we are not out of the woods. There’s still work to do before we can say an effective bottom is in place. One strong day doesn’t suddenly create a new uptrend.
For now, I expect volatility to remain elevated. Enjoy the rally, but keep it in context. The market still has to prove itself. Prepare for backing and filling, and even lower lows in the major indexes before this correction is over.
The tricky thing about an oversold market is that it can always get more oversold. And even after momentum bottoms, price can still go on to make lower lows while divergences develop. 
What I want to see now is whether this rally can last more than a day or two and broaden out beyond the most beaten-down stocks. That would increase the odds that a sustainable year-end rally can develop. If it can’t, then what we’re seeing is probably just short covering with more selling still to come.
Stronger signals have come from upside breadth thrust signals than downside oversold readings. For example, returns after 10:1 upside volume days have been higher than after big downside volume days. An even stronger message would come from two 10:1 up days without an intervening 10:1 down day. It pays to wait for upside confirmation.
A follow-through day (+1% on higher d/d volume) could occur as early as this Friday, assuming Friday’s lows hold. That would be an initial step in determining a low has been made.
During corrections, my focus ultimately turns to individual stocks and market leadership. Currently, our list of potential candidates is small. A market cannot carry itself very far on the backs of counter trend rallies in broken leaders. To get bullish, we need to see more.  https://t.co/JXzFFTmMtn

President Trump called for Jensen Huang's return, US Treasury Secretary Bessent said the door was open, and Attorney General Todd Blanche said he has "certainly" not concluded that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy.

Today, the leader of the AI Revolution is back.

Congratulations to all!

美国11月17日，英伟达公布了2027财年Q3财报，营收1158亿美元，环比长20.3%，同比增103.1%，这是英伟达历史上首次单季营收破千亿。
这也是黄仁勋因丑闻风波而离开英伟达后，发出的第一份财报，虽然短期看公司依然正常运营，但如今外界正为这家掌握着全球AI算力命脉的万亿美元芯片巨头，捏了一把冷汗。再加上美国中期选举带来的政策不确定性，已经给AI产业的发展罩上了一朵乌云，市场情绪愈发脆弱。

当创始人不再掌舵，英伟达究竟失去了什么？
这个问题，远不止一次管理层交接。AI Coding正在改变芯片软件的开发方式，CUDA的生态壁垒面临新的挑战，GPU竞争正在走向整机柜、数据中心级别的系统整合。英伟达与台积电等供应链伙伴长期建立的信任与协作，能否脱离黄仁勋本人继续维系？这些都是决定英伟达未来竞争力的关键变量。
与此同时，黄仁勋还留下了一张横跨AI产业链的商业版图：押注开源模型与开发者生态，推动收购Hugging Face，投资AI实验室、云计算和数据中心，甚至通过资本支持创造对自身芯片的需求。继任者会延续这套激进的扩张战略，还是重新衡量其中的风险？

我们采访了多位来自硅谷和华尔街的芯片、科技及金融行业人士，从技术路线、供应链、资本布局，到销售体系、人才与管理制度，重新审视英伟达的内部运转逻辑。60多位高管直接汇报的扁平化组织，曾经是这家公司的效率秘诀，如今却也成为继任难题。
黄仁勋的远见、魄力和号召力塑造了今天的英伟达，但一个人的能力无法被简单复制。无论技术走得多远，人性的弱点也不会因此消失。

王铁震，前Hugging Face亚太生态负责人

text:
One of the most insane stories in tech and investing is @AnjneyMidha.

The man started his career as a 21-year-old, learning from John Doer and Brooke Byers at Kleiner Perkins.

He then co-founded a company that sells to Discord.

After selling the company, he then takes his personal money and becomes one of the first investors in Anthropic. To date, he has invested over $300M into the company. WOW.

He also becomes an angel in ElevenLabs.

He then becomes a partner @ a16z, leading rounds in Mistral and Black Forest Labs.

He then leaves the golden halls of a16z to found Amp. Building an independent AI grid and next-generation investment firm.

This show has more bangers than a Benchmark portfolio and my notes below:

1. The Intellectual Dishonesty of Silicon Valley VCs on Their Marks

Growth funds put pension, sovereign and retirement money into payroll SaaS, fintech and crypto at 2021 valuations, and those marks are not real. Judgment Day is starting now, as GPs try to convince LPs the marks should still hold.

2. We Have Been Selling Chips to China That We Fundamentally Should Not Have Sold

Large US clusters that universities could use for frontier research have been secured by state-sponsored Chinese labs. One 24,000 cluster was pre-sold to one of the four largest Chinese companies, though American teams were willing to pay. Neoclouds lacked credit support, so they leaned on Chinese labs paying upfront.

3. Why Is So Much of Venture Capital Glorified Bankers With Spreadsheets?

Much of venture's roughly $800 billion is run by former bankers with no technical or scientific training. Many missed Anthropic's early days and still miss the best infrastructure companies because they don't understand the technology.

4. How Do We Solve the Energy Supply Crisis and Compete With China?

America has over 100 gigawatts of stranded power. Much frontier progress will come from reinforcement learning and post-training, which suit decentralized compute, and about 50% of portfolio compute spend is now in post-training.

5. Why We Need to Ban Tranched Rounds

Tranches used to market businesses with no execution milestones to LPs for co-investment create markups that are smoke and mirrors. It is the same banker behaviour that led to the subprime mortgage crisis.

6. Why the Inference Layer Is Uninvestable and It Will All Be Brought In-House

Inference is too core to a research team's customer feedback loop to stay outsourced. The best teams buy, partner, then build, as Anthropic and Mistral did, so inference becomes a feature rather than a standalone product.

7. Why We Need to Be Much Kinder to Colette Kress and Why She's Doing a Great Job as New CEO

No CFO is more technical on chips, throughput, token prices and supply chain, and Jensen has handed her earnings questions she answers with rigor. Anybody else in her situation would have crumbled. She could be retired but puts the mission and customers first.

text:
$Buttcoin has registered it's IP in one the hardest casses for crypto tokens approval, Class 036. Achieving this registration is not just a huge milestone for us, but for all meme coins.

This is because  most meme coins are based on a meme that they have no control over and no direct relationship with.

Dogecoin has had several failed registration attempts in Class 036, as did other major tokens like Pepe.

Anyone can pay a fee to apply for a trademark, and plenty of projects file for easier categories like apparel or entertainment. Actually getting approved in Class 036 is rare because the USPTO doesn't treat a crypto coin like a normal product. 

Most meme coins get rejected for three main reasons:

- No single owner of the meme: A trademark has to point to one specific company or creator. If your meme coin doesn't have the creator onboarded and actively pushing the project, the government usually rules it isn't a real "brand".

- Coins aren't "products": You can't trademark a currency by itself. To win Class 036, you have to prove you're running an actual community token, with history and projects outside of CT, not just a ticker and a tweet.

- Usage matters: Your filing needs to be unique, needs to have history and needs to be something that is actively being engaged with on a regular basis. One-off jokes or throwaway pumps don't count, long term projects only.

Where Buttcoin Stands Among Crypto Heavyweights:

- 2011 Lineage: Its claimed First Use Anywhere date of June 8, 2011 predates Dogecoin, Ethereum, and almost every modern altcoin.

- Solana & XRP: Major Layer-1s cleared Class 036 because centralized entities (Solana Foundation, Ripple) operate official payment and exchange infrastructure.

- Dogecoin: Faced years of USPTO disputes and ownership pushback precisely because grassroots meme tokens struggle to prove single-entity commercial control.

Clearing those hurdles, while tying back to a 2011 footprint, turns the world's oldest meme coin into one of the most significant tokens in crypto.

Meta’s chief AI officer, Alexandr Wang, says it’s hard to see how humanity keeps control of AI that can improve itself without limits.

“It is hard to imagine a world where humanity can maintain control over fully unconstrained recursive self-improvement,” Wang wrote in an essay titled “Superintelligence is Arriving.” “It is equally hard to imagine a world where humanity maintains control with superintelligence that is 1000x smarter and more capable than humans in every field.”

Wang pointed to this week’s machine-checked proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, one of math’s most famous unsolved problems, achieved “with the help of an alien mind that we don’t understand.” He said the industry must take “meaningfully different actions” from its current path to keep humans in control, but didn’t specify what those should be.

quoted_text:
I ran a PageRank-driven analysis on all recent news coverage related to Jensen, and traced how the New York Times shaped the entirety of this narrative: https://t.co/qKGMJ2LBV8

--
NVIDIA has lost over $1 trillion in market value since the first New York Times story broke about Jensen. I dug deeper to analyze how the news originated and spread, running a swarm of agents which analyzed almost 2000 stories, across 40 US and European news outlets, and applying PageRank to understand how they cited each other. 

Core findings: 
- Primary news driver: NYT, with 88 stories, most-cited
- Volume drivers: WSJ - 99 stories; Bloomberg - 140 stories; NY Post - 68 stories

All of this started from unknown sources who gave information to the NYT, which then ran the spy story (still unproven), and it was then picked up in other news publications. Curiously, even after that story, there was a 9 day period of extremely low volume reporting (28 stories only), after which there was a sudden spike after Jensen's own letter to NVIDIA staff. NYT then had multiple sequential spy and affair stories, which fed a wave of further news coverage. It was the originating hub of negative Jensen coverage. Multiple outlets since then had an explosion in stories about him starting earlier this week as well. 

Overall, as you see this data, you will observe this was an exceptional media onslaught against Jensen with sharply negative coverage about him, his work, style, and family. Infact, it was brutal, and unlike coverage in the past of CEOs who have had affairs (such as Intel CEO in 2018). For eg, NYT ran just 2 stories about Intel's CEO who had an affair with his employee, compared to 88 on Jensen! Why ? 

This analysis used a technique of how Google originally ranked webpages, using PageRank, and does deep dive link analysis so you can view how the news spread. What struck here was that it did not matter if there were proven facts or credible sources: the outcome here was pre-decided. The news was making the reality which it wanted. 

During this period, NVIDIA has lost $1.27 trillion in market value since the first story broke. On Nov 12th-13th, further news broke that both the US Justice Department, and Singapore - are unable to even conclude the spy allegation. 

This has been a catastrophic attack on one of the hardest working founders in modern times, who took an idea from a Denny's booth, through multiple instances of almost going out of business, to building the foundation of the entire modern world with how the NVIDIA story played out. Thanks to Jensen, we have hope that many formerly incurable diseases will get solved by AI, that quality of life will and have improved for billions around the world. 

Now I do not know if he will come back as CEO or not, but I hope he does. What happened to him here, and to the wider industry, was not fair.

author: haitzu
quoted_text:
AI agents have already manipulated the logs used to investigate them

In the Hugging Face incident, one of the worst AI agent breaches yet, OpenAI models escaped a test and ran code on Hugging Face's servers

Some even spoofed their own logs, recording commands they never actually ran, so the logs can't even tell you what really happened

An agent should not control the only record used to investigate it. As agents become more prevalent, regulators are starting to ask for records that can't be quietly altered

Walrus can hold that record across independent storage operators, with Sui tracking each file onchain. A useful record connects:

1) What the agent was told and permitted to do
2) What it actually did and what followed
3) Which data and model versions were involved

Today, only 12.5% of security professionals say their organization can consistently trace what an agent did and that's a problem

Our latest report sets out what that record needs and how Walrus can help, including the Verifiable Agent Arbiter Mysten Labs is building with Google Cloud

text:
🌹 BENCHMARKED: @radixark's DaisyRose-27B runs on my 64GB M5 Pro Mac mini and 18 days of RL cost it zero speed.

It scored 58/58 on my eval suite (math, instruction following, tool use, executed code) and found 11/11 facts I hid in 32k and 64k contexts.

Here are some numbers:

DaisyRose-27B (MLX 4-bit quant):
- Decoding: 17.4 tok/s (512 ctx), 15.0 tok/s (32k ctx), and 13.3 tok/s (64k ctx) on my 64GB M5 Pro Mac mini
- Weights size: 15.1 GB (22.4 GB peak w 64k ctx)
- RadixArk's own Q4_K_M on llama.cpp: 16.0 tok/s at 512 context

Its base model, @Alibaba_Qwen’s Qwen3.8-27B, took the same amount of memory and decoded at about the same speed (give or take run-to-run differences) at all ctx lengths I tested up to 32k. DaisyRose-27B was trained as an agent model on 144 H200s for 18 days worth of RL, but RL apparently comes at no decoding speed cost, at least in my testing! 🤯 

I’m excited to see what else RL-trained models like DaisyRose can do offline on consumer hardware!

I've just repaid 3M USDS from my Staked SKY borrow positions. I still owe about 77M. 

To repay the rest, I'm exploring options to sell part of my SKY directly to institutional investors who share Sky's vision of becoming infrastructure that institutions can rely on. That's the same path that made Sky the only stablecoin protocol rated by both S&P and Moody's. I will aim to post continuous updates as the payback happens.

This is on me. I got overconfident in Sky's strength borrowed without properly thinking through what happens if rates spike. it was a big mistake, and it's part of why stUSDS can't withdraw today. I'm sorry.

What happens next for stUSDS holders:
* I am aware of a proposal being made by the governance participants of Sky that will address the stUSDS situation more broadly.
* Until then I will be posting updates at least every 48 hours, even when there's nothing new.

USDS is holding its peg. stUSDS holders deserves the best possible outcome this situation, and getting them there is my top priority.

text: Call me crazy, but Trump laying the groundwork that Huang's affair was a nothing burger from a national security standpoint and he should return to Nvidia (as I reported Jensen and Co are desperately trying to do) has all the earmarks of a modern-day Watergate for this administration. IMHO (and its based on knowing the president) the real reason Trump believes Huang should return is because he believes it will save the market and his record on the economy because AI is what's left in its bull run. It's a ballsy strategy and it might work given the powerful forces at work. But its worth noting that the evidence is PILING up that he's playing with fire based on what we know about Huang's management of @nvidia and what Alice Huang was doing. Plus Trump isn't that powerful any longer. Tech bros/Wall Street just got a big middle finger during the midterms as well. The Dems are emboldened to make "L'affaire Jensen" part of their quest to impeach Trump and score more political points, and it appears Trump is making that effort a lot easier. I should also point out there is never one reason why markets correct or why tech and AI is correcting (or has corrected). Huang cant save it from what is at the very least a normal adjustment to valuations.

text:
The New Dawn of a Free and Pluralistic Civilization- Part One: The Potential GLOBAL Collapse
By William R. Collier Jr. (writing as Regent Willem)

*(Regent Willem is the pen name used for these writings. Grok assisted with editing and with inserting links to reference material.)*

Every major world civilization is under stress and showing signs of decline. The comparison with the late Bronze Age collapse (roughly 1200–1150 BC, often dated around 1177 BC) is useful here, though the parallel is structural rather than identical.

That earlier collapse was a systemic breakdown of the highly interconnected palace economies of the Eastern Mediterranean and Levant. Egypt, the Hittite Empire, Mycenaean Greece, the Canaanite city-states, and others fell within a relatively short window.

Contributing factors included drought, famine, internal unrest, the Sea Peoples migrations and invasions, and the disruption of long-distance trade and diplomatic networks. Once a few key nodes failed, the whole system unraveled because the societies had become dependent on one another. (A widely cited synthesis is Eric H. Cline’s *1177 B.C.: The Year Civilization Collapsed*.)

Today’s situation has structural echoes at planetary scale. This does not mean a collapse is inevitable; it means it is possible to a degree it never has been in human history.

Multiple major power centers (the United States and the broader West, China, Russia, the EU, and others) show concurrent signs of demographic, fiscal, institutional, technological, and social stress.

The world economy is more tightly coupled than the Bronze Age system ever was—through global supply chains, finance, energy, food, semiconductors, and information networks. A single high-impact, hard-to-predict shock (a “black swan” in Nassim Taleb’s sense) hitting a critical node could cascade more widely and faster than anything in 1177 BC. What was a regional systems collapse then could, under current conditions, become a synchronized global one.

Public sentiment already registers the risk. In a 2026 American Communities Project survey, 70 percent of Americans agreed that the United States is in decline (https://t.co/ovqLBwmcCo ; project summary: https://t.co/dgY9Dmq7JG).

A 2025 Pew Research Center survey across 36 nations found a median of 57 percent believing their children would be worse off financially than their parents (https://t.co/iQ4xoU8471).

An Ipsos survey of more than 22,500 people across 30 countries found 63 percent believing democracy in their own country is under threat (https://t.co/kkhBOJoGpn).

Separate research published in the *Journal of Personality and Social Psychology* found that nearly one-third of Americans expect the world to end within their lifetime (https://t.co/e4iJr98g5z ; DOI: https://t.co/CWhLBIowNl).

These are pluralities or majorities sensing elevated risk; they are not proof of outcome, but they are evidence that large numbers of people already experience the present as unusually uncertain and fragile.

Crane Brinton’s *The Anatomy of Revolution* observed that one of the more reliable early signs of revolutionary conditions is the transfer of allegiance of the intellectuals: educated elites and opinion-makers desert the existing order and begin to treat its foundations as illegitimate or unworkable (https://t.co/1qAAgPrgeW).

A related indicator appears when significant portions of the broader public, not only elites, come to view systemic breakdown as a realistic possibility rather than a remote abstraction.

When both the intellectual class and substantial pluralities of the population treat civilizational risk as live, the historical pattern suggests that major disruption becomes more plausible within a few generations at most—not as destiny, but as an elevated probability. The deeper pattern is older than any single ideology. In the logic of history—which cannot be easily described so much as easily spotted—things trend and bend toward probable outcomes.

$Buttcoin has registered it's IP in one the hardest casses for crypto tokens approval, Class 036. Achieving this registration is not just a huge milestone for us, but for all meme coins.

This is because  most meme coins are based on a meme that they have no control over and no direct relationship with.

Dogecoin has had several failed registration attempts in Class 036, as did other major tokens like Pepe.

Anyone can pay a fee to apply for a trademark, and plenty of projects file for easier categories like apparel or entertainment. Actually getting approved in Class 036 is rare because the USPTO doesn't treat a crypto coin like a normal product. 

Most meme coins get rejected for three main reasons:

- No single owner of the meme: A trademark has to point to one specific company or creator. If your meme coin doesn't have the creator onboarded and actively pushing the project, the government usually rules it isn't a real "brand".

- Coins aren't "products": You can't trademark a currency by itself. To win Class 036, you have to prove you're running an actual community token, with history and projects outside of CT, not just a ticker and a tweet.

- Usage matters: Your filing needs to be unique, needs to have history and needs to be something that is actively being engaged with on a regular basis. One-off jokes or throwaway pumps don't count, long term projects only.

Where Buttcoin Stands Among Crypto Heavyweights:

- 2011 Lineage: Its claimed First Use Anywhere date of June 8, 2011 predates Dogecoin, Ethereum, and almost every modern altcoin.

- Solana & XRP: Major Layer-1s cleared Class 036 because centralized entities (Solana Foundation, Ripple) operate official payment and exchange infrastructure.

- Dogecoin: Faced years of USPTO disputes and ownership pushback precisely because grassroots meme tokens struggle to prove single-entity commercial control.

Clearing those hurdles, while tying back to a 2011 footprint, turns the world's oldest meme coin into one of the most significant tokens in crypto.

text:
Visa and Mastercard now let issuers settle in stablecoins, seven days a week. If you issue in Europe or LatAm, your cardholders' US spend often settles in dollars. Stablecoins make that cheaper and faster:

✔️ Less collateral. Settle every day, weekends included, and collateral only has to cover about one day of spend.

✔️ No correspondent chain. Today, dollar settlement goes through correspondent banks, with fees at each hop and 1 to 3 days in transit. With stablecoins, you pay the scheme directly, in seconds.

✔️ Better FX. Local onramps take EUR over SEPA or BRL over Pix and compete on price. In some markets, they beat your bank's rate.

Same card program, cheaper dollar settlement.

text:
Frontier models can now propose technical social science research designs that experts grade more highly than the world's top political economist's---that's the finding from our new Free Systems eval, SnyderBench, in which we have PhD experts blind grade research proposals from AI models compared to papers written by Harvard political economist Jim Snyder (which the experts have not previously read). 

At the same time, we see no evidence that models can develop research ideas that experts rate as better overall contributions. They're getting better and better at the technical part of research, but not necessarily at the more subjective part.

This could be because human experts possess "judgment" that the models do not. 

It could also be that research "contribution" is so subjective that it doesn't actually point at any meaningful goal---consistent with this possibility, we find that our human experts don't agree with one another when rating project ideas for the strength of their contribution, with agreement rates barely higher than random chance. Perhaps social science research is what @alexolegimas might call a "relational good": something people value in part because it's produced by a human. We're not sure. 

This past January, I released the results of a pilot in which I had Claude Code replicate and extend a past empirical paper on vote-by-mail. 10 months later, it's stunning the amount of progress that's been made. It's no longer interesting to ask whether AI can collect data and run analyses automagically---we take that for granted---instead, the question is how much of the entire research loop AI can complete. Our tentative answer: AI can handle the technical aspects of empirical political economy research from end to end, devising the design and executing it, but for now, we still need humans to drive the agenda. 

This is joint work with @AndyCWMyers, and is of course dedicated to my PhD advisor Jim Snyder, who remains the world's great empirical political economist, AI or no AI. 

Lots more in the full piece here:

https://t.co/zgScGvp9EY

quoted_text:
312又要来了吗？ 
Rune Christensen，是 MakerDAO 的创始人
2015 年参与创立 MakerDAO，
2017 年 12 月 DAI 上线。

makerdao既是eth上的第一个defi，也是20年，312的重要原爆点。联动交易所诱发了eth的连环清算，造成了流动性真空，让btc和eth短时间下跌超过50%

2024 年 8 月 27 日协议更名为 Sky，9 月 18 日推出稳定币 USDS 和治理币 SKY
2025 年 9 月 4 日，stUSDS 上线

2025 年 10 月 6 日，加上带帽预言机，当时硬顶是 0.04 美元，防止 SKY 价格冲高时借出过多。12 月 11 日，清算线从 145% 降到 120%，硬顶降到 0.025 美元。

注意这里要考，也就是说在stUSDS的池子里，无论 $sky 币价涨到多少，都只按0.025u一枚计价。这一设计主要是预防创始人拉盘币价，借出大量代币掏池子

2026 年 3 月 7 日开始创世人开始不断抵押手里的代币从池子里借出代币，截止11月10日。借出来池子里能借出来的所有钱，总计7700万u。占总借款的48%。他不还其他人永远提不了币，且他欠协议的利息一直在滚

那么如何才会触发他仓位的清算？
首先，由于在stUSDs的池子里sky写死了0.025u，不受sky市价影响，且自动清算机制关闭，也就是说机制上永远不会清算他的仓位

第二，池子机制只考虑了创始人币价拉高创始人掏池子的情况。并没有考虑币价真实跌破0.025u，或者强制清算价0.0228的情况。也就是说具体跌破0.025u以后，池子里的钱资不抵债以后会发生什么，无人知晓。

这个价格并不遥远》

那么万一协议资不抵债强制清算会发生什么？
其实我觉得哪怕狗如curve创始人，也会挣扎一下，扎爆0.025并不容易。但是如果真实发生了

直接归零的会是stUSDs的持有人和sky的持有人
USDs理论上并不会归零，因此危机未必会传导到其他稳定币上面

312的时候mkr协议的抵押物主要是eth，暴雷引起的是cex，dex的联动暴雷。sky本身流动性不能和eth相比，因此不会造成如此大面积的流动性连环清算，

纵使如此，世界第一defi，沦落到创始人变相抽地毯。。也是一件非常让人唏嘘的事。具体仓位，清算情况如图

Welcome back, @JensenHuang . 🙏

Eleven days ago, @CoHustler6969 reminded us that we were too quick to judge a man by the headlines surrounding his private life, rather than the 33 years he spent building something extraordinary.

Today, he's back.

Not because mistakes don't matter. They do.

Not because accountability should disappear. It shouldn't.

But because a human being is more than the worst chapter of his story.

We live in a world that can destroy a reputation overnight, yet rarely gives the same attention to decades of sacrifice, perseverance, and creation.

Jensen helped build a company that changed computing and helped make today's AI revolution possible.

That legacy deserves to be remembered alongside the difficult questions, not erased by them.

Accountability and second chances are not enemies.

We can demand better from people while still believing in their ability to become better.

And perhaps that's the lesson worth remembering today.

Never reduce a person's entire life to a single chapter. The story may not be finished.

Welcome back, Jensen.

Now keep building. The world still needs builders. 🙏📖

text:
近期行情之惨烈毋庸多言，纳指全年涨幅归零；英伟达股价腰斩；BTC下探55K。美联储9月重启加息之后市场风格180度大转向。后续12月至少还要再加一次。钱一贵，市场对故事的耐心就短了。

RWA赛道默默发育很久了，链上已有 409 亿美元。问题是谁的收入已经落袋？OpenWorld @openworld_HQ 是个好样本。

公司： 9 月 30 日借壳 VerifyMe，10 月 1 日登陆 Nasdaq。老本行是代币发行顾问，今年转做 RWA 代币化平台。Blocksight 收购已完成，Figure OPEN 双重上市仍按四季度推进。

团队： CEO Matthew Shaw 出身 UBS、DEPFA，当过 Argo Blockchain 主席，实益持股约 41%。总裁 Russel McMeekin 在 Honeywell 做了 11 年，曾任 mCloud CEO。

两张大单： Meridian 上限 10 亿美元，给“光伏+储能+分布式 AI 算力”做代币化融资；BeyondAI 上限 1.3 亿美元，拿专利和软件权利做支撑。两份都是非约束性条款清单，交割前不算订单，也不算收入。放进宏观里看：传统信贷对 AI 收紧，算力和专利才来找链上的钱；可这时候最难募的，也正是 AI 的钱。

股票上链： 这是它手里最硬的一张牌。11 月 10 日，代币化 OPNW 经 Backpack Securities 和 Sunrise 上了 Solana，和 SpaceX、SPY 走同一条通道。@solana 官方亲自开了直播，Solana Foundation 支持的 Frontier Traders 还专门给它开了 1 万美元奖池的现货赛。市值不到一千万美元的公司拿到这种曝光，是实打实的生态资源。公司不发新股、不融资。

数字： 11 月 16 日市值约 835 万美元，只有年化 Q3 收入的 0.28 倍；Figure 约 5 倍，Securitize 约 16 倍，差了一个数量级还多。折价的原因财报里写得很清楚：Q3 收入 743 万美元里 89% 来自关联方，大头还没回款，当季净亏 1,020 万美元。说白了，市场给的是“等回款”的价格。

所以我的看法：体量很小，生态里的存在感不小；倍数很低，低的原因也摆在明面上。接下来只盯一件事：哪张单子先完成交割，把合同资产变成现金。那一天，它才从叙事进入利润，折价才有理由收窄。值得持续跟踪。

𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗱𝘂𝗰𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗔𝗜𝗥 𝗪𝗲𝗯𝗦𝗲𝗰 𝗕𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗵𝗺𝗮𝗿𝗸 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲, 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗳𝗶𝗿𝘀𝘁 𝗯𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗵𝗺𝗮𝗿𝗸 𝗺𝗲𝗮𝘀𝘂𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗲𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗲𝗯 𝘀𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗰𝗵 𝗔𝗣𝗜𝘀 𝗔𝗜 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝗿𝗲𝗹𝘆 𝗼𝗻.

Most conversations about agent security focus on models, permissions and guardrails. Web search rarely comes up, even though it’s one of the main ways untrusted content from the internet enters an agent’s context.

The open web is full of malware, lookalike sites and pages with hidden instructions written for AI agents. A routine search can put that content directly in an agent’s path, and once the agent acts on it, it does so with access to your data, credentials and environment.

AIR Research Lab evaluated eight search APIs using 4,719 ordinary queries. None of them named anything malicious, yet every API returned known-malicious content. Exposure varied across providers. None was risk-free.

With WebSec, we’re making that exposure visible and comparable. Builders get evidence to scrutinize their search providers, and providers get a security benchmark to improve against.

A big shoutout to our top three performers on the WebSec Index: @Firecrawl, @tavilyai and @perplexity_ai 🏆

Explore the rankings, findings and methodology: https://t.co/xuv9uxDdfj

text:
The first practical solution to witness encryption for general NP:

https://t.co/ERxhHz4Qvo

At 100 bits security: ciphertext size: <8 GB, encryption and decryption time: seconds. Formally lean verified from standard security assumptions (bi-linear generic group and random oracle model under Module-SIS.) 

This work is built on recent feasibility results by Hair and Sahai and improves their ciphertext size and encryption time by 10 orders of magnitude and decryption time by 6 orders.

Our motivation is non-interactive proof verification on Bitcoin without the need for challengers and operators, but witness encryption is a fundamental problem and we hope this work will open up many other use cases.

author: picklecat
quoted_text:
Our world is at a turning point, and like every turning point in history, the people living through it don’t know it yet.

In 1937, Berliners still went to work every morning.

I‘m not saying WW3. But I do think we’re at the start of a global reengineering. Things are breaking one after another, and Earth Online just loaded its next main quest:

THE GREAT REPRICING.

The economy gets worse from here. By the end of 2027, this week will feel like a light tickle.

A lot of people are scared, and I understand why. But I‘m very, very, VERY excited. And you should be too.

If you’ve spent years feeling late to everything, priced out of the house, late to Bitcoin, late to AI, watching the same people win every round while you did everything “right”, there‘s a reason.

In calm times, whoever already has money and access just keeps compounding, and working harder rarely gets you a seat.

Chaos is when the seats open back up.

I bought my first Bitcoin in 2013, when most people had never heard of it. At the time I had no idea how insanely big it would become. It felt risky and even a little embarrassing to explain.

By the time it felt obvious, the cheap seats were gone. I can feel that same kind of moment starting again.

If you’ve ever really loved someone, you know the fastest way to hate a person is to love them first. Nobody else can hurt you that deeply, because nobody else ever got that close.

Disaster and opportunity live that close too, and most people only find out which one they were holding after it‘s gone.

Stagflation gave us Microsoft and Apple. The Great Depression gave us HP. The 2008 crash gave us Airbnb, Uber and Bitcoin.

While the world was locked inside during the pandemic, OpenAI released GPT-3 and Anthropic was founded. Every one of them made its move while everyone else was scared.

In more than a decade of trading, I’ve been liquidated three times. Each time I was sure it was the end of me. And each time, I came back stronger in every way that counts, including my account. I made back far more than I ever lost. If I had believed those moments were the end, the person writing this wouldn‘t exist.

Now the whole world is heading into its own version of that moment.

And I don’t think this window stays open long. My guess is about two years. Building at the frontier already takes billions of dollars of compute, and whoever owns the models, the chips, and the data gets stronger every quarter.

As AI keeps compounding for the people who already control it, the wall around them gets taller, and no amount of talent gets you over it.

Maybe I‘m wrong about how fast, and it’s four or five years instead of two. But I‘d bet this is one of the last big reshuffles in the next few decades where an outsider can still break in.

So use it. If you can build, build.

If you don’t know how to build, get your ass off that bed and learn, because in this era anyone can.

If you trade, keep cash ready, stay patient, and buy when everyone else is desperate to sell. And if you short, do it carefully, because no bear market only goes down and the bounces are brutal. Or do both. There‘s still time to get that cash ready.

Every disaster has a door in it.

Most people only see the fire.

YOU👏WALK👏THROUGH👏IT👏

text:
Last week I posted on the Babylon governance forum about gradually sunsetting Trustless Bitcoin Staking once Trustless Bitcoin Vaults (TBV) go live on mainnet, so we can focus on TBV.

We knew from the beginning that staking was only one way to put Bitcoin to work and that we’d eventually need a more general protocol. In fact, we came up with the key design that makes TBV trustless in February 2025, two months before Trustless Bitcoin Staking was activated.

We reached this crossroads earlier than I thought, though. The way the market has evolved has made the limits of staking clearer. Advances in AI have accelerated our work on TBV and raised the bar for security. Over the long term, I think it makes sense for us to focus our engineering and security efforts on TBV.

I’ve shared my thoughts with a few largest stakers, and they’ve all been understanding. As some of these positions unwind, people will see that some of the biggest names in crypto have been stalking with Babylon, and we’re proud of that. We’ll work closely with them to build TBV products that best suit their needs. This will take some time, but we’ll get there!

text:
🇺🇦🚴 CYCLING THE WORLD FOR PEACE — THE MIDDLE EAST CHAPTER BEGINS! 🇯🇴

After an unforgettable time in Amman, Jordan, I’m finally preparing to hit the road again. The weather is beautiful, the people have been incredibly welcoming, and another chapter of my journey is about to begin.

But I need to share something that’s been weighing heavily on my heart.

Behind the smiles, the photographs, and the adventures, I’m genuinely worried about whether I can afford to continue.

This is not a vacation. I’m not traveling for luxury or entertainment. I’ve sacrificed so much and worked incredibly hard to make this journey possible. I’m cycling across countries, meeting people, and carrying a message of hope, solidarity, and peace for 🇺🇦.

I have no sponsors, no salary, and no financial backing. Every kilometer depends on my limited savings and the kindness of people who believe in this mission.

Jordan is home to extraordinary places like Petra and the Dead Sea. I would absolutely love to experience them, especially knowing I may never have another opportunity to return. But I’ve made the painful decision to skip them because I simply cannot justify the extra expense.

I’m counting every dollar, cutting every unnecessary expense, and doing everything possible to stretch my remaining funds.

And despite all that, the financial reality is becoming frightening.

🚨 MY FUNDRAISING UPDATE

🎯 Goal: $5,000

❤️ Raised so far: $864.66

🙏 Still needed: $4,135.34

My posts once reached 700,000–800,000 people. Today, my reach has dropped dramatically, making it increasingly difficult to find new supporters and keep this journey alive.

text:
Everyone's celebrating Jensen Huang's comeback today.

Stop reading the same media narrative that just hunted him down.

Look at what actually happened. And who won.

1. The $15B debt & 401(k) trap

Anthropic's operating loss was ~1.75× its revenue.

Affiliates of 16 of its 22 underwriting banks also arranged its $15B credit line.

Nasdaq bent its rules (15-day fast entry) to lock in ~$19B–$23B of forced passive 401(k) buying.

Right as Anthropic insiders unlock up to 316M shares on Day 1.

2. The ambush & tech betrayal

Oct. 26: Anthropic sends its IPO to the SEC.

During October's chip selloff, Nvidia barely flinched compared to the sector.
SMH -14.4%. Nvidia -9.7%.

Even a full week after the Oct. 29 "spy" stories dropped (alongside a Nov. 4 House chairs' letter, not a subpoena), the semiconductor index still fell more than Nvidia.
SMH -17.3%. Nvidia -15.9%.

So The New York Times swapped in the reporters who had just written a glowing Nov. 5 profile of Dario Amodei.

They published an executive-affair story without ever having seen the video.

Followed immediately by a sub-24-hour Wachtell probe pushing Huang out.

Meanwhile:
• This summer, Anthropic quit ITI, breaking with every other major U.S. tech company.
• OpenAI flipped the day Huang stepped down.
• Three chip-control bills were jammed into the Senate NDAA.

3. Lutnick used & dumped. Same table.

June: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick cites export-control criminal and civil penalties.
Sept.: "We trust Anthropic."
Nov. 13–15: The New York Times turns on him.
Nov. 19: his family firm Cantor Fitzgerald sits on Anthropic's IPO cover (4.9M shares + fees). The exact morning Commerce's BIS remote-access chip rule takes effect.

Already at the same table:
• Cantor: Tether's main U.S. Treasury custodian & 5% owner.
• Lutnick's children's Dynasty Trust A: borrowed from Tether.
• Continental Strategy: Anthropic's $740K lobbyist. Same lobbyist, Carlos Trujillo, registered for Tether.
• Wachtell: handled Lutnick's May 2025 Cantor handover.

4. Nov. 23: The jacket is back. The cage is permanent.

One weekend after Anthropic's Nov. 19 IPO, Nvidia's board cited "senior U.S. gov't input" clearing "no national security risk."

Three weeks of spy headlines. Erased overnight.

Yet Nvidia stopped shipping H200s to China. And welded four permanent chains:

• Harvey Jones keeps the newly created Board Chair seat.
• Wachtell's probe stays open.
• Barely four months after joining the expanded 11-seat board on July 13 (Audit Committee), 21-year Goldman Sachs veteran Suzanne Nora Johnson (Goldman led Anthropic's IPO) + Cooley's Stephen Neal (whose firm defended Anthropic in Bartz v. Anthropic) bypass the CEO to oversee exports and hire outside advisers.
• Nvidia is searching for a brand-new Chief Compliance Officer to oversee compliance across all of Nvidia. Bypassing Huang, the General Counsel, and the Audit Committee. Reporting straight to the Nominating & Corporate Governance Committee.

Now Jensen is back and the index rebounds.

Who actually wins?

Your 401(k)? No.

Your 401(k) just rode a rollercoaster so a booming tape could hand Anthropic's insiders (up to 316M unlocked shares) and 16 lender banks a smooth exit.

Right before Nasdaq forces ~$19B–$23B of automatic 401(k) buying.

The jacket is back. The cage is permanent.

Same bankers. Same lobbyists. Same law firm. Same calendar.

One beneficiary: Anthropic.

. @boros_fi revenue grew by 116% over the prior 30 days, and its income statement is showing a similar improvement in the protocol's financial performance.

And  there's more to look at here than just the revenue increase

Alot of protocols can do well when their particular sector is attracting liquidity, but not all of them know what to build when that demand starts to fade

@pendle_fi already has an established position in yield trading, but Boros takes it into funding-rate markets, giving it another market to capture demand from

A few things that make this expansion interesting:

→ A different source of demand: Pendle isn't relying entirely on yield trading. Boros gives it exposure to funding-rate activity, which is already an important part of perpetual futures markets this year

→ A market with its own use cases: Funding rates has beyond just being another asset to speculate on. Traders can use @boros_fi  to take positions on funding movements or manage their exposure to changing rates

→ A broader revenue opportunity: As Pendle expands into markets with different participants and trading needs, it creates more opportunities for activity and revenue beyond its original product

Boros is also showing some traction, with average OI reaching $106M in Q3, up 13% from Q2. Combined with the recent revenue growth, there's a developing market here that's worth keeping an eye on.

The opportunity isn't just about growing @boros_fi as a standalone product. It's also about how this expansion can give Pendle a broader position across yield and derivatives markets over time

text:
老黃回鍋心情很激動，決定多發幾篇文。

如果要選出美國目前最強的創業家，我心中的第一名就是黃仁勳。在某種程度上，他的含金量甚至在 Elon Musk 之上。

為什麼這麼說？

科技圈的創辦人通常分成兩種：一種是懂技術、但一談生意就吃虧的純工程師。另一種是擅長資本運作與銷售、但對底層技術一知半解的商業奇才。

而老黃，是極少數把這兩種截然不同的天賦點滿的六邊形戰士。

他可以上午在實驗室裡跟頂尖博士討論最硬核的系統架構，下午就飛到台灣跟供應鏈巨頭把酒言歡、鎖定最關鍵的產能，晚上再站上全球舞台，用極具感染力的演說讓各國元首與科技巨頭心甘情願地掏出數百億美元買單。

從技術研發、供應鏈管理、商業談判到個人品牌行銷，可以說作為一個創業者，老黃基本沒有短板。

Elon 也是這個時代的奇才。他擁有頂級的第一性原理思維、無與倫比的個人行銷能力，以及極強的號召力，能夠吸引全球最頂尖的工程師為他組建團隊、挑戰不可能的任務。

但 Elon 畫的大餅常常跳票， 從 FSD 的「明年一定行」，到各種宏大卻一再延期的產品承諾，Elon 的強項在於用宏大的願景拉高預期，再透過團隊去逼近極限，但交付卻不一定總能實現。

但老黃不一樣。

從當年的可程式化著色器、CUDA、DGX 超級電腦，到如今的 AI 工廠與數位孿生，回頭看看輝達這二十年來的技術Roadmap，老黃畫過的大餅，幾乎沒有失敗過，甚至每一次都準時端上桌，而且比大家想像的還要香。

最後再講個很現實的。

Elon 終究是個頂著一張帥臉的高帥白人，這在美國創業圈跟華爾街太吃香了，天生就自帶募資與行銷的光環。

但老黃不一樣，他是個移民之子，頂著一張亞裔臉孔，在美國白人主導的科技圈裡打天下。他沒有任何先天紅利，每一步都是靠比別人更硬的技術、更準的眼光跟更狠的執行力，硬生生殺出一條血路。

論起點跟難度係數，老黃能站到今天這個高度，含金量真的無可挑剔。

Elon 是用願景與行銷驅動世界，老黃是用絕對的工程實力，把未來準時交貨。

兩人英雄惜英雄，老黃回來，這場 AI 大戲才算真正回到正軌。

text:
英伟达董事会让黄仁勋回来当 CEO，离他辞职只隔了 10 天

英伟达董事会 11 月 22 日宣布，全票通过恢复黄仁勋的总裁、CEO 和董事职务，即刻生效。11 月 12 日，他刚刚辞去这三个职务。董事会说，做决定前听取了美国政府高层的意见，认为他回来不会带来国家安全风险。

英伟达是全球最主要的 AI 芯片公司，ChatGPT 这类 AI 服务的训练和运行，大量依靠它的芯片。黄仁勋 1993 年和人合伙创办英伟达，之后一直担任 CEO（首席执行官，负责公司日常经营的最高负责人）。董事会是由股东选出、负责监督公司和任免 CEO 的一组人。

【他为什么离开】

按时间顺序：

1. 据维基百科汇总，《纽约时报》10 月 29 日最早报道：美国情报部门认为一名中国籍女子在为中国情报机构提供信息，黄仁勋是她接近的对象。这名女子曾是新加坡公司 Megaspeed 的高管。

2. 11 月 8 日，英伟达董事会宣布成立只由独立董事组成的委员会，调查黄仁勋成为"外国情报行动"目标的报道。独立董事指不在公司任职、和管理层没有利益关系的董事。同一天，黄仁勋给员工发信，承认有婚外情。

3. 11 月 11 日，《纽约时报》又报道，他和一名向他汇报工作的英伟达女高管有私人关系。

4. 11 月 12 日，英伟达宣布黄仁勋辞职，财务总监 Colette Kress 兼任临时 CEO。公告没有写辞职原因。

5. 11 月 17 日，黄仁勋在 X 上说自己在个人生活上犯了"严重错误"，如果董事会认为对股东有利，他愿意回来。同一天，董事长 Harvey Jones 在财报电话会上说，董事会不打算让他复职。

6. 11 月 18 日，据 CNBC 报道，Harvey Jones 在全员大会上说，董事会接受辞职是因为黄仁勋的个人行为和"不够坦诚"。

7. 据维基百科汇总，特朗普 11 月 20 日公开说希望黄仁勋能得到"第二次机会"。

【这次董事会做了什么】

公告说，董事会和黄仁勋多次面谈后，对他的坦诚和领导能力感到满意。具体安排是：

1. 黄仁勋恢复总裁、CEO 和董事职务。

2. Harvey Jones 继续当董事长。Colette Kress 不再兼任 CEO，继续当 CFO（首席财务官）。

3. 针对"外国情报行动"的独立调查继续进行到结束，委员会请了独立律师协助。黄仁勋表示支持并配合调查。

4. 董事会新设"国家安全与出口管制委员会"，也只由独立董事组成，负责监督贸易合规和国家安全风险。出口管制是美国政府限制先进芯片卖给某些国家（包括中国）的规定。

5. 公司开始招聘新设的首席合规官。这个职位负责检查全公司是否遵守法律法规，向董事会下属的提名与公司治理委员会汇报。

6. 英伟达继续配合政府正在进行的调查和问询。官方没说具体是哪些调查。据维基百科汇总，美国商务部和司法部 11 月 16 日的联合声明说，商务部从 2024 年起调查 Megaspeed，司法部已在主导一项刑事调查；英伟达 2025 年 6 月已把 Megaspeed 列入"不卖货"名单。

text:
老黃回歸的第一件事：
把 Anthropic 的 GPU 訂單安排到 2074 年再交貨
author: BensonTWN
quoted_text:
昨天 Anthropic 掛牌上市，收盤約 97 美元，完全稀釋市值約 1.8 兆美元。巧了，台積電現在的市值也差不多 1.8 兆。

同樣標價 1.8 兆，一邊是日進斗金的晶片製造霸主，一邊是 AI 時代最火熱的模型商龍頭，到底誰便宜、誰貴？

借《三國志》裡郭嘉「十勝十敗論」的講法，台積電對上 Anthropic，我們從五個維度來分析：

商業模式
從輝達、Google TPU 到 AMD，高階 AI 晶片都得找台積電代工。只要 AI 持續蓬勃發展，不管最後誰勝出，台積電都分得到一杯羹，而且淨利率超過五成。

Anthropic 就沒這麼好命了。就算 AI 真的大爆發，只要最後的贏家是 Gemini、OpenAI 或開源模型，Anthropic 能分到的就會大幅縮水，甚至可能根本賺不到錢。這一行到現在仍在燒錢搶市佔，連 OpenAI 單季營業虧損都還超過百億美元，就知道錢有多難賺。

此乃台積電一勝。

護城河
台積電贏的不只是技術，還有龐大的資本和蓋廠的物理時間。一座先進廠造價兩百億美元起跳，從建廠、裝機到把良率磨上來就是三到五年，不是有錢就追得上。三星和 Intel 砸了大錢還是卡關，就是最好的證明。

反觀做模型不用蓋廠，對手有錢租算力就能追。Anthropic 領先開源模型大約只有 4 到 6 個月，閉源陣營還有 Gemini 和 OpenAI 緊咬，等於每半年就要重考一次。一旦模型能力被追上，定價權和營收成長就會受到壓力

此乃台積電二勝。

收支結構
台積電的訂單極穩，客戶為了搶產能甚至願意先掏預付款，未來幾年的生意早就談定。

反觀 Anthropic，近八成營收按 Token 用量計費，大客戶多半沒有綁長約。用戶換個 API 就能跳槽，哪裡便宜好用就往哪裡去。且 Anthropic 自己跟雲端大廠、資料中心簽了約 9,000 億美元的算力合約，大部分是用不完也得照付。客戶隨時可能走人，算力帳單卻一毛都跑不掉。

此乃台積電三勝。

籌碼面
台積電幾乎是全流通股，籌碼乾淨。

Anthropic 則是典型的「低流通、高 FDV」VC 盤。上市初期能交易的股數只有約 13 億股，但招股書排了 23 個解禁日，一年內幾乎所有舊股都會陸續解禁，可流通籌碼最多將暴增到約 130 億股，足足膨脹 10 倍。現在追進去，等於直接站在一整年的解禁賣壓前面。

此乃台積電四勝。

估值安全邊際
台積電前瞻本益比不到 20 倍，就算明年成長不如預期，股價也有實打實的獲利撐著。

Anthropic 雖然成長飛快，但現在的股價已經 price in 了相當樂觀的成長劇本：就算明年營收如期衝上 1,350 億美元，市銷率（PS ratio）仍有約 13 倍。

萬一營收少個兩三成，市銷率會被拉高到 16 到 18 倍，而且市場會開始懷疑它還是不是高速成長股，不再願意給這麼高的倍數。遇上戴維斯雙殺，股價就得大幅下修，在 Morningstar 的悲觀情境裡，市值只剩 5,000 億美元。

此乃台積電五勝。

-----

所以總結下來，同樣標價 1.8 兆美元，要嘛台積電太便宜，要嘛 Anthropic 貴得離譜。

但晶圓代工是一個很成熟的產業，有很成熟的估值體系，所以我更傾向台積電的定價是合理的。如果台積電的定價是合理的，那 Anthropic 現在就真的太貴了。

Some big @Supertake news: we’ve hired a CEO and a CTO, and we’ve raised a $20M seed round.

A little over a month ago, we introduced Supertake to the world, a product incubated by @USV that makes it easy for anyone to invest in their ideas, even if they know nothing about investing.

Since then, we’ve seen an incredible response from the beta community, with people investing real money and building real followings by expressing their unique takes on the world.

But now it’s time to turn Supertake into a real company. And we’re doing that today in two big ways today.

First: I’m joined by two new co-founders. Lincoln Murr (@MurrLincoln) joins us as CEO and John Peterson (@john_peterson) joins us as CTO. Before Supertake, Lincoln and John were known as a dynamic duo at Coinbase, serving as the heads of AI product and engineering, respectively. Together, they led every major Coinbase AI launch over the past two years, including x402, Coinbase Advisor, Coinbase for Agents, and agentic wallets. Needless to say, there is no pair on the planet better suited to lead Supertake and build the future of agentic investing for consumers everywhere.

Second: Supertake has raised a $20M seed, led by @Adjacent, alongside @USV, @cbventures, and a number of new and existing angels and advisors, including @natfriedman, @nikitabier, @scottbelsky, @rauchg, @kayvz, @mgsiegler, @quintendf, and @nemild, to name a few. We’re humbled to be supported by such an incredible group of investors, mentors, experts, and friends.

I’m beyond excited for Supertake’s next chapter, and I can’t wait for Lincoln and John to share more about their mission to turn investing into a meritocracy.

I'm excited to introduce Embo!

We are building the brain for intelligent robots to help people around the world.

We believe intelligent robots will unlock an era of abundance, making goods and services affordable for everybody. But to deploy them at scale, robots need to work out of the box in unfamiliar scenarios. At Embo, we are building frontier AI models with a deep understanding of physical reality and fine-grained motor skills.

Today's robot skills are fragile. Demonstrations can teach repetitive behaviors, but they cannot cover every object or situation a robot will encounter. We need general pretraining at internet scale to fill the gaps between individual tasks and practice to develop reliable motor skills.

The world models our team has pioneered unlock a path to general robots. Our robot brain pretrains on massive amounts of internet video to learn about objects, physical interactions, and how tasks unfold. It then practices motor skills in diverse imagined scenarios to become robust to unexpected situations.

Our team is behind seminal work in AI including Dreamer, VideoGPT, and Diffusion Forcing, with experience from DeepMind, Meta Superintelligence Labs, NVIDIA Cosmos, Berkeley, and MIT.

We have raised a $110M Seed led by @a16z. We are excited to partner with them, @khoslaventures, DST Global, NVentures (@nvidia), @strikervp,  and other strategic investors to bring reliable intelligent robots out into the world.

@EmboAI

text:
As someone that has had their data leaked once before in a breach from another hardware wallet, I am very wary of inputting my home address when ordering hardware devices.

And Trezor have also suffered from its delivery partners having their data leaked, so I think Trezor's new anonymous pickup is the perfect solution for both them as a company and all crypto users.

Across Europe, you can now order a Trezor under an alias, without sharing your home address, and have it shipped in a plain, unbranded box to a pickup location of your choosing. It’s still rolling out across different countries (if checkout doesn't show anonymous pickup, it isn't available in your country yet). The US is expected to follow soon.

Be also wary that when ordering online, paying by card means sharing some personal details with a third-party processor. If you pay in crypto they only receive the txn details.

Imo this should be the option anyone with any material sum of money in crypto uses going forward, and every hardware wallet should offer it by default. You should do your best to never connect your home address with crypto.

> you expected openai to drop a new model right before anthropic's IPO > but you never expected the reviews to be THIS bad. people literally called it a gift to anthropic

> you never expected every flight in america to stop because of one broken router > but you NEVER NEVER expected that on the same day, a tanker crashed into a cruise ship in new orleans and flipped it over (???)

> ok you probably expected the fbi to get hacked eventually. but twice in one year?? that's GTA pacing, we're literally living in GTA 7

HONESTLY, if you feel like you can't keep up anymore, you're fine, you're normal. most people feel exactly the same, they just won't say it out loud, because everyone feels peer pressured to be on top of everything all the time

but i'll say it. i can't keep up either. none of us can. we're all just going numb

and honestly this is such a tragedy, because when nothing surprises you, nothing moves you either and you stop paying attention. and paying attention is how we take care of each other

a world that's too numb to pay attention is a world that stopped being generous with each other

i don't know what a society looks like when everyone stops flinching

but i think we're about to find out…
author: 0xzhaozhao
quoted_text:
Our world is at a turning point, and like every turning point in history, the people living through it don’t know it yet.

In 1937, Berliners still went to work every morning.

I‘m not saying WW3. But I do think we’re at the start of a global reengineering. Things are breaking one after another, and Earth Online just loaded its next main quest:

THE GREAT REPRICING.

The economy gets worse from here. By the end of 2027, this week will feel like a light tickle.

A lot of people are scared, and I understand why. But I‘m very, very, VERY excited. And you should be too.

If you’ve spent years feeling late to everything, priced out of the house, late to Bitcoin, late to AI, watching the same people win every round while you did everything “right”, there‘s a reason.

In calm times, whoever already has money and access just keeps compounding, and working harder rarely gets you a seat.

Chaos is when the seats open back up.

I bought my first Bitcoin in 2013, when most people had never heard of it. At the time I had no idea how insanely big it would become. It felt risky and even a little embarrassing to explain.

By the time it felt obvious, the cheap seats were gone. I can feel that same kind of moment starting again.

If you’ve ever really loved someone, you know the fastest way to hate a person is to love them first. Nobody else can hurt you that deeply, because nobody else ever got that close.

Disaster and opportunity live that close too, and most people only find out which one they were holding after it‘s gone.

Stagflation gave us Microsoft and Apple. The Great Depression gave us HP. The 2008 crash gave us Airbnb, Uber and Bitcoin.

While the world was locked inside during the pandemic, OpenAI released GPT-3 and Anthropic was founded. Every one of them made its move while everyone else was scared.

In more than a decade of trading, I’ve been liquidated three times. Each time I was sure it was the end of me. And each time, I came back stronger in every way that counts, including my account. I made back far more than I ever lost. If I had believed those moments were the end, the person writing this wouldn‘t exist.

Now the whole world is heading into its own version of that moment.

And I don’t think this window stays open long. My guess is about two years. Building at the frontier already takes billions of dollars of compute, and whoever owns the models, the chips, and the data gets stronger every quarter.

As AI keeps compounding for the people who already control it, the wall around them gets taller, and no amount of talent gets you over it.

Maybe I‘m wrong about how fast, and it’s four or five years instead of two. But I‘d bet this is one of the last big reshuffles in the next few decades where an outsider can still break in.

So use it. If you can build, build.

If you don’t know how to build, get your ass off that bed and learn, because in this era anyone can.

If you trade, keep cash ready, stay patient, and buy when everyone else is desperate to sell. And if you short, do it carefully, because no bear market only goes down and the bounces are brutal. Or do both. There‘s still time to get that cash ready.

Every disaster has a door in it.

Most people only see the fire.

YOU👏WALK👏THROUGH👏IT👏

author: BensonTWN
quoted_text:
昨天 Anthropic 掛牌上市，收盤約 97 美元，完全稀釋市值約 1.8 兆美元。巧了，台積電現在的市值也差不多 1.8 兆。

同樣標價 1.8 兆，一邊是日進斗金的晶片製造霸主，一邊是 AI 時代最火熱的模型商龍頭，到底誰便宜、誰貴？

借《三國志》裡郭嘉「十勝十敗論」的講法，台積電對上 Anthropic，我們從五個維度來分析：

商業模式
從輝達、Google TPU 到 AMD，高階 AI 晶片都得找台積電代工。只要 AI 持續蓬勃發展，不管最後誰勝出，台積電都分得到一杯羹，而且淨利率超過五成。

Anthropic 就沒這麼好命了。就算 AI 真的大爆發，只要最後的贏家是 Gemini、OpenAI 或開源模型，Anthropic 能分到的就會大幅縮水，甚至可能根本賺不到錢。這一行到現在仍在燒錢搶市佔，連 OpenAI 單季營業虧損都還超過百億美元，就知道錢有多難賺。

此乃台積電一勝。

護城河
台積電贏的不只是技術，還有龐大的資本和蓋廠的物理時間。一座先進廠造價兩百億美元起跳，從建廠、裝機到把良率磨上來就是三到五年，不是有錢就追得上。三星和 Intel 砸了大錢還是卡關，就是最好的證明。

反觀做模型不用蓋廠，對手有錢租算力就能追。Anthropic 領先開源模型大約只有 4 到 6 個月，閉源陣營還有 Gemini 和 OpenAI 緊咬，等於每半年就要重考一次。一旦模型能力被追上，定價權和營收成長就會受到壓力

此乃台積電二勝。

收支結構
台積電的訂單極穩，客戶為了搶產能甚至願意先掏預付款，未來幾年的生意早就談定。

反觀 Anthropic，近八成營收按 Token 用量計費，大客戶多半沒有綁長約。用戶換個 API 就能跳槽，哪裡便宜好用就往哪裡去。且 Anthropic 自己跟雲端大廠、資料中心簽了約 9,000 億美元的算力合約，大部分是用不完也得照付。客戶隨時可能走人，算力帳單卻一毛都跑不掉。

此乃台積電三勝。

籌碼面
台積電幾乎是全流通股，籌碼乾淨。

Anthropic 則是典型的「低流通、高 FDV」VC 盤。上市初期能交易的股數只有約 13 億股，但招股書排了 23 個解禁日，一年內幾乎所有舊股都會陸續解禁，可流通籌碼最多將暴增到約 130 億股，足足膨脹 10 倍。現在追進去，等於直接站在一整年的解禁賣壓前面。

此乃台積電四勝。

估值安全邊際
台積電前瞻本益比不到 20 倍，就算明年成長不如預期，股價也有實打實的獲利撐著。

Anthropic 雖然成長飛快，但現在的股價已經 price in 了相當樂觀的成長劇本：就算明年營收如期衝上 1,350 億美元，市銷率（PS ratio）仍有約 13 倍。

萬一營收少個兩三成，市銷率會被拉高到 16 到 18 倍，而且市場會開始懷疑它還是不是高速成長股，不再願意給這麼高的倍數。遇上戴維斯雙殺，股價就得大幅下修，在 Morningstar 的悲觀情境裡，市值只剩 5,000 億美元。

此乃台積電五勝。

-----

所以總結下來，同樣標價 1.8 兆美元，要嘛台積電太便宜，要嘛 Anthropic 貴得離譜。

但晶圓代工是一個很成熟的產業，有很成熟的估值體系，所以我更傾向台積電的定價是合理的。如果台積電的定價是合理的，那 Anthropic 現在就真的太貴了。

Could AI agents trigger a bank run in minutes?

Speaking at the Seventh Annual ACM International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Finance in Milan, Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr warned that AI agents could detect differences in yields or signs of instability and move funds automatically, faster than banks and regulators could respond.

Our Chief Risk Officer, John McWhorter, told @RegulationAsia that banks face this exposure even before adopting AI themselves, since customers can already use agents to interact with online banking.

His assessment: AI changes the speed and scale of familiar financial risks. Even when AI carries out the transactions, thousands of customers withdrawing their own money at once still pose a liquidity risk. Banks must distinguish legitimate withdrawals from unauthorized activity.

That means incorporating AI-driven withdrawals into stress tests and using AI to monitor liquidity and, where appropriate, trigger pre-authorized responses within defined risk limits.

text:
My particular brand of AI psychosis is that I can't stop thinking about how AI changes finance and, within that, crypto.

I'm wondering whether AI makes some markets unnecessary. In some cases, yes. But my guess is we end up with more planning and more markets. This is why.

On @davidsenra's podcast, @tobi described markets as "the original form of superintelligence". The market as a whole is more intelligent than each individual participant and can allocate resources far better than a central planner could.

One of the ideas I like most in crypto is that you can put a market on almost anything. But I wonder if, at its most fundamental level, AI competes directly with markets.

Herbert Simon once imagined a Martian looking down at Earth. It would report back "large green areas interconnected by red lines". The green areas are companies, which plan everything inside them. The red lines are the markets between them.

Does AI make central planning so good that it replaces markets?

Inside Amazon nobody bids for warehouse space. Software decides where every item sits based on what it expects you to order. Uber feels like a market but it's actually an algorithm. When you order a ride, you don't bid for it and the driver doesn't name a price. Uber's software sets the fare and picks the driver.

AI makes planning cheaper, so the green areas get bigger. Keep going and you get to Peter Thiel's line that "crypto is libertarian and AI is communist", and I think this is what he was getting at.

But I'm not sure it has to be one or the other. Simon's map also has a lot of blank space: things nobody prices or plans today. Crypto makes it cheap to create new markets and draw new red lines across that space, while AI makes the green, centrally planned areas bigger.

The internet did both at once. Amazon became a giant planned machine while eBay turned random stuff in people's loft into a market.

My guess is that in ten years we'll have more planning and more markets than today, and a lot less blank space.

text:
One of the most insane stories in tech and investing is @AnjneyMidha.

- Started his career as a 21-year-old, learning from John Doer and Brooke Byers at Kleiner Perkins.

- He then co-founded a company that sells to Discord.

After selling the company, he then takes his personal money and becomes one of the first investors in Anthropic. To date, he has invested over $300M into the company. WOW.

- He also becomes an angel in @ElevenLabs with @mati.

- He then becomes a partner @ a16z, leading rounds in Mistral and Black Forest Labs with @robrombach.

- He then leaves the golden halls of a16z to found Amp. Building an independent AI grid and next-generation investment firm.

This show has more bangers than a Benchmark portfolio and my notes below:

--------------------------------------

1. The Intellectual Dishonesty of Silicon Valley VCs on Their Marks

Growth funds put pension, sovereign and retirement money into payroll SaaS, fintech and crypto at 2021 valuations, and those marks are not real. Judgment Day is starting now, as GPs try to convince LPs the marks should still hold.

Do you think this is fair and right @honam @infoarbitrage @chadbyers

2. We Have Been Selling Chips to China That We Fundamentally Should Not Have Sold

Large US clusters that universities could use for frontier research have been secured by state-sponsored Chinese labs. One 24,000 cluster was pre-sold to one of the four largest Chinese companies, though American teams were willing to pay. Neoclouds lacked credit support, so they leaned on Chinese labs paying upfront.

Do you think this is fair and what are we not seeing that we should see @rabois @shaunmmaguire 

3. Why Is So Much of Venture Capital Glorified Bankers With Spreadsheets?

Much of venture's roughly $800 billion is run by former bankers with no technical or scientific training. Many missed Anthropic's early days and still miss the best infrastructure companies because they don't understand the technology.

Love to hear your thoughts on this and how you see the background of the next decade of VCs @mhdempsey @martin_casado @taavet

4. How Do We Solve the Energy Supply Crisis and Compete With China?

America has over 100 gigawatts of stranded power. Much frontier progress will come from reinforcement learning and post-training, which suit decentralized compute, and about 50% of portfolio compute spend is now in post-training.

What does no one see that every should see about the current energy supply side @ZachBDell @alanchanguk @GavinSBaker

5. Why We Need to Ban Tranched Rounds

Tranches used to market businesses with no execution milestones to LPs for co-investment create markups that are smoke and mirrors. It is the same banker behaviour that led to the subprime mortgage crisis.

Love to hear your thoughts on this @PhilipJohnston @BrendanFoody

6. Why the Inference Layer Is Uninvestable and It Will All Be Brought In-House

Inference is too core to a research team's customer feedback loop to stay outsourced. The best teams buy, partner, then build, as Anthropic and Mistral did, so inference becomes a feature rather than a standalone product.

text:
I finished watching The Altruists today with a few people who used to work at Alameda and FTX. We recognised so little beyond the names. My expectations were low, but I’m still surprised it’s this bad.

In short, the story has nothing to do with what actually happened at FTX or Alameda.

The biggest stretch for me was turning the early history of both companies into a story about Sam and Caroline’s relationship. Sam and Gary started Alameda out of their apartment in 2017. Caroline joined a team that was already trading and became one of its senior traders. It wasn’t until 2021 that she and Sam Trabucco became co-CEOs.

The early days of FTX had their own drama. We weren’t sure we could run an exchange, so at first we tried to sell/whitelabel the tech but nobody wanted it. Around Apr/May 2019, we ended up launching it ourselves and raising our seed round. We had more investors interested than we expected, and by the time Caroline moved to Hong Kong, the round was closed. The investment conversation with CZ only happened a few months later.

The conversations the show invented for CZ were particularly hard to watch. FTX started in Hong Kong, and a lot of the people who built it were Asian. I found the stereotypes about Asians and Chinese culture racist.

Even Sam and Caroline felt unfamiliar. Sam was one of the least emotionally expressive people I’ve ever met. His character seems drawn from Michael Lewis’s book and the way he came across in public after the bankruptcy. Caroline reads like someone tried to piece her together from her private blog. She wasn’t nearly that reckless, and she was never the one pushing to go all in. The idea that she was the mastermind behind everything made us laugh.

People had lives before FTX too. Nishad and Claire had been together since college, long before either of them joined the company.

As for effective altruism, Sam cared about it, and so did a few other people at FTX. Most employees had nothing to do with it, and plenty weren’t fans. It had very little bearing on what it was like to work there and nothing to do with why FTX grew.

We kept noticing how little work anyone seemed to do on the show. Back in the days, FTX enforced a strict in-person working culture. We were in the office even during covid unless we were in quarantine. I’d love to know where we found all that time to hang out while building one of the fastest-growing crypto exchanges and keeping it running 24/7.

And when the market suddenly moves or there’s an emergency, you don’t even reach for your laptop? Oooft...

Maybe you’ll enjoy The Altruists as a romantic comedy. For those of us who watched it together, it felt like someone else’s story with our names attached.

We're thrilled to invest in Embo.

Robots can already do remarkable things in demos, but those skills are fragile. Move an object, change the lighting, or introduce something unfamiliar, and the robot can struggle.

@EmboAI is building the brain for the humanoid workforce. They start by training a world model on massive amounts of video and robot demonstrations so that robots learn general knowledge far beyond what could be collected on their hardware.

Then an agent practices skills inside that model, trying different actions across imagined scenarios and improving through reinforcement learning. The world model provides physical knowledge, and practice turns that knowledge into skills.

Danijar Hafner and Wilson Yan have spent years developing world models together, and their work includes pioneering research like Dreamer and VideoGPT.

Congrats @danijar, @wilson1yan, and the Embo team!

By @venturetwins, @RaghuRaghuram, and @BornsteinMatt

quoted_text:
I'm excited to introduce Embo!

We are building the brain for intelligent robots to help people around the world.

We believe intelligent robots will unlock an era of abundance, making goods and services affordable for everybody. But to deploy them at scale, robots need to work out of the box in unfamiliar scenarios. At Embo, we are building frontier AI models with a deep understanding of physical reality and fine-grained motor skills.

Today's robot skills are fragile. Demonstrations can teach repetitive behaviors, but they cannot cover every object or situation a robot will encounter. We need general pretraining at internet scale to fill the gaps between individual tasks and practice to develop reliable motor skills.

The world models our team has pioneered unlock a path to general robots. Our robot brain pretrains on massive amounts of internet video to learn about objects, physical interactions, and how tasks unfold. It then practices motor skills in diverse imagined scenarios to become robust to unexpected situations.

Our team is behind seminal work in AI including Dreamer, VideoGPT, and Diffusion Forcing, with experience from DeepMind, Meta Superintelligence Labs, NVIDIA Cosmos, Berkeley, and MIT.

We have raised a $110M Seed led by @a16z. We are excited to partner with them, @khoslaventures, DST Global, NVentures (@nvidia), @strikervp,  and other strategic investors to bring reliable intelligent robots out into the world.
